16.4.d: यद् अश्नासि यत् पिबसि धान्यं कृष्याः पयः । आद्यं यद् अनाद्यं सर्वं ते अन्नम् अविषं कृणोमि ॥
16.4.m: Whatever you eat, whatever you drink, / grain of agriculture, milk, / what is eatable and what is uneatable, / all your food I make poisonless.

16.4.s: ahne ca tvā rātraye ca ubhābhyāṃ pari dadhmasi | arāyebhyo jighatsubhya imaṃ naḥ pari rakṣata ||
16.4.d: अह्ने च त्वा रात्रये च उभाभ्यां परि दध्मसि । अरायेभ्यो जिघत्सुभ्य इमं नः परि रक्षत ॥
16.4.m: To both day and night / we entrust you; / from greedy Arāyas / do you two protect this man for us!

16.5.s: śataṃ te 'yutaṃ hāyanā dve yuge trīṇi catvāri santu | indrāgnī viśve devā anu manyantām ahṛṇīyamānāḥ ||
16.5.d: शतं ते ऽयुतं हायना द्वे युगे त्रीणि चत्वारि सन्तु । इन्द्राग्नी विश्वे देवा अनु मन्यन्ताम् अहृणीयमानाः ॥
16.5.m: May a hundred, ten thousand years be yours, / two ages, three, four! / May Indra and Agni, all the gods / grant approval without being angry!

16.5.s: śarade tvā hemantāya vasantāya griṣmāya pari dadhmasi | varṣāṇi tubhyaṃ syonāni yeṣu vardhanta oṣadhīḥ ||
16.5.d: शरदे त्वा हेमन्ताय वसन्ताय ग्रिष्माय परि दध्मसि । वर्षाणि तुभ्यं स्योनानि येषु वर्धन्त ओषधीः ॥
16.5.m: To autumn, to winter, to spring, / to summer we entrust you; / may the rainy seasons be pleasant for you, / in which the plants grow!

16.5.s: mṛtyur īśe dvipadāṃ mṛtyur īśe catuṣpadām | tasmāt tvā mṛtyor gopater ud dharāmi sa mā mṛthāḥ ||
16.5.d: मृत्युर् ईशे द्विपदां मृत्युर् ईशे चतुष्पदाम् । तस्मात् त्वा मृत्योर् गोपतेर् उद् धरामि स मा मृथाः ॥
16.5.m: Death rules over two-footed creatures; / death rules over four-footed creatures; / from death, the lord of herds, / I lift you up; do not die!

16.5.s: so 'riṣṭa na mariṣyasi na mariṣyasi mā bibheḥ | na vai tatra pra mīyante no yanty adharaṃ rajaḥ ||
16.5.d: सो ऽरिष्ट न मरिष्यसि न मरिष्यसि मा बिभेः । न वै तत्र प्र मीयन्ते नो यन्त्य् अधरं रजः ॥
16.5.m: Uninjured, you will not die; / you will not die, do not fear! / Truly they do not perish there, / nor do they go to the lower darkness.

16.5.s: sarvo vai tatra jīvati gaur aśvaḥ puruṣaḥ paśuḥ | yatredaṃ brahma kriyate paridhir jīvanāya kam ||
16.5.d: सर्वो वै तत्र जीवति गौर् अश्वः पुरुषः पशुः । यत्रेदं ब्रह्म क्रियते परिधिर् जीवनाय कम् ॥
16.5.m: Truly everyone lives there— / cow, horse, man, beast— / where this sacred prayer is made / as an enclosure for life.

16.5.s: pari tvā pātu samānebhyo 'bhicārāt sabandhubhyaḥ | amamrir bhavāmṛto 'tijīvo mā te hāsiṣur asavaḥ śarīram ||
16.5.d: परि त्वा पातु समानेभ्यो ऽभिचारात् सबन्धुभ्यः । अमम्रिर् भवामृतो ऽतिजीवो मा ते हासिषुर् असवः शरीरम् ॥
16.5.m: May it guard you from your peers, / from sorcery, from your relatives! / Become immortal, surviving long; / may your vital breaths not leave your body!

16.5.s: viśve tvā devā amṛtena bibhratv adhivaktā paśupatiṣ ṭe astu | anāmayat savitā te kṛṇotv ā tvā prāṇo viśatu jīvanāya ||
16.5.d: विश्वे त्वा देवा अमृतेन बिभ्रत्व् अधिवक्ता पशुपतिष् टे अस्तु । अनामयत् सविता ते कृणोत्व् आ त्वा प्राणो विशतु जीवनाय ॥
16.5.m: May all the gods maintain you with immortality; / may Paśupati be your advocate! / May Savitṛ make you free from disease; / may breath enter into you for life!

16.5.s: ye mṛtyava ekaśataṃ yā nāṣṭrātijīvyā | muñcantu tasmāt tvā devā agner vaiśvānarād adhi ||
16.5.d: ये मृत्यव एकशतं या नाष्ट्रातिजीव्या । मुञ्चन्तु तस्मात् त्वा देवा अग्नेर् वैश्वानराद् अधि ॥
16.5.m: The deaths that are a hundred and one, / the destruction that must be outlived— / from that may the gods release you, / away from Vaiśvānara Agni!

16.6.s: rakṣohaṇaṃ vājinam ā jigharmi mitraṃ prathiṣṭham upa yāmi śarma | śiśāno agniḥ kratubhiḥ samiddhaḥ sa no divā sa riṣaḥ pātu naktam ||
16.6.d: रक्षोहणं वाजिनम् आ जिघर्मि मित्रं प्रथिष्ठम् उप यामि शर्म । शिशानो अग्निः क्रतुभिः समिद्धः स नो दिवा स रिषः पातु नक्तम् ॥
16.6.m: I smear the demon-slaying courser with butter; / I approach the widest friendship, protection. / Agni, sharpened, kindled by sacred acts, / may he protect us by day, from harm by night!

16.6.s: ayodaṃṣṭrān arciṣā vāvṛdhānān upa spṛśa jātavedaḥ samiddhaḥ | ā jihvayā mūradevān rabhasva kravyādo vṛṣṭvāpi dhatsvāsan ||
16.6.d: अयोदंष्ट्रान् अर्चिषा वावृधानान् उप स्पृश जातवेदः समिद्धः । आ जिह्वया मूरदेवान् रभस्व क्रव्यादो वृष्ट्वापि धत्स्वासन् ॥
16.6.m: Kindled, O Jātavedas, / touch with your flame the iron-toothed [demons] as they grow great! / Seize the root-worshiping demons with your tongue; / having torn the flesh-eaters, place them into your mouth!

16.6.s: ubhobhayāvinn upa dehi daṃṣṭrā hiṃsraḥ śiśāno 'varaṃ paraṃ ca | utāntarikṣe pari yāhy agne jambhaiḥ saṃ dhehy abhi yātudhānān ||
16.6.d: उभोभयाविन्न् उप देहि दंष्ट्रा हिंस्रः शिशानो ऽवरं परं च । उतान्तरिक्षे परि याह्य् अग्ने जम्भैः सं धेह्य् अभि यातुधानान् ॥
16.6.m: Knowing both, set your jaws to work, / harmful, sharpening the lower and the upper [jaw]! / And travel around in the atmosphere, O Agni; / crush the sorcerers between your teeth!

16.6.s: agne tvacaṃ yātudhānasya bhindhi hiṃsrāśanir harasā hantv enam | pra parvāṇi jātavedaḥ śṛṇīhi kravyāt kraviṣṇur vi cinoty enam ||
16.6.d: अग्ने त्वचं यातुधानस्य भिन्धि हिंस्राशनिर् हरसा हन्त्व् एनम् । प्र पर्वाणि जातवेदः शृणीहि क्रव्यात् क्रविष्णुर् वि चिनोत्य् एनम् ॥
16.6.m: O Agni, pierce the skin of the sorcerer; / may the harmful thunderbolt slay him with heat! / Break his joints, O Jātavedas; / may the raw-flesh-eating vulture tear him apart!

16.6.s: yajñair iṣūḥ saṃnamamāno agne vācā śalyām̐ aśanibhir dihānaḥ | tābhir vidhya hṛdaye yātudhānān pratīco bāhūn prati bhaṅdhy eṣām ||
16.6.d: यज्ञैर् इषूः संनममानो अग्ने वाचा शल्याँ अशनिभिर् दिहानः । ताभिर् विध्य हृदये यातुधानान् प्रतीचो बाहून् प्रति भङ्ध्य् एषाम् ॥
16.6.m: Bending your arrows with sacrifices, O Agni, / anointing your arrow-heads with speech and lightning-bolts, / with them pierce the sorcerers in the heart; / break their arms backwards!

16.6.s: yatredānīṃ paśyasi jātavedas tiṣṭhantam agna uta vā carantam | utāntarikṣe patantaṃ yātudhānaṃ tamasā vidhya sarvā śiśānaḥ ||
16.6.d: यत्रेदानीं पश्यसि जातवेदस् तिष्ठन्तम् अग्न उत वा चरन्तम् । उतान्तरिक्षे पतन्तं यातुधानं तमसा विध्य सर्वा शिशानः ॥
16.6.m: Wherever now you see [one], O Jātavedas, / standing, O Agni, or walking, / or flying in the atmosphere, the sorcerer, / pierce him with darkness, sharpening all [your weapons]!

16.6.s: utārabdhāc chṛṇīhi jātaveda utārebhāṇād ṛṣṭibhir yātudhānāt | agne pūrvo ni jahi śośucāna āmādaḥ kṣviṅkās tam adantv enīḥ ||
16.6.d: उतारब्धाच् छृणीहि जातवेद उतारेभाणाद् ऋष्टिभिर् यातुधानात् । अग्ने पूर्वो नि जहि शोशुचान आमादः क्ष्विङ्कास् तम् अदन्त्व् एनीः ॥
16.6.m: Break [him] from the beginning, O Jātavedas, / and from the grasping sorcerer with your spears! / O Agni, blazing forth, strike him down first; / may the screeching raw-eaters devour him, the speckled ones!

16.6.s: iha pra brūhi yatamaḥ so agne yo yātudhāno ya idaṃ śṛṇoti | tam ā rabhasva samidhā yaviṣṭha nṛcakṣasaś cakṣuṣe randhayaitam ||
16.6.d: इह प्र ब्रूहि यतमः सो अग्ने यो यातुधानो य इदं शृणोति । तम् आ रभस्व समिधा यविष्ठ नृचक्षसश् चक्षुषे रन्धयैतम् ॥
16.6.m: Declare here which one he is, O Agni, / who is a sorcerer, who hears this! / Seize him with your kindling stick, O youngest one; / deliver him to the eye of the men-watcher!

16.6.s: tīkṣṇenāgne cakṣuṣā rakṣa yajñaṃ prāñcaṃ vasubhyaḥ pra ṇaya pracetaḥ | hiṃsraṃ rakṣāṃsy abhi śośucānaṃ mā tvā dabhan yātudhānā nṛcakṣaḥ ||
16.6.d: तीक्ष्णेनाग्ने चक्षुषा रक्ष यज्ञं प्राञ्चं वसुभ्यः प्र णय प्रचेतः । हिंस्रं रक्षांस्य् अभि शोशुचानं मा त्वा दभन् यातुधाना नृचक्षः ॥
16.6.m: With a sharp eye, O Agni, protect the sacrifice; / lead it forward to the Vasus, O wise one! / Blazing against the harmful demons, / may the sorcerers not harm you, O men-watcher!

16.6.s: nṛcakṣā rakṣaḥ prati paśya vikṣu tasya trīṇi prati śṛṇīhy agrā | tasyāgne pṛṣṭīr harasā śṛṇīhi tredhā mūlaṃ yātudhānasya vṛśca ||
16.6.d: नृचक्षा रक्षः प्रति पश्य विक्षु तस्य त्रीणि प्रति शृणीह्य् अग्रा । तस्याग्ने पृष्टीर् हरसा शृणीहि त्रेधा मूलं यातुधानस्य वृश्च ॥
16.6.m: As a men-watcher look upon the demon among the clans; / break off his three tips! / Break his ribs with heat, O Agni; / cut the sorcerer's root threefold!

16.7.s: trir yātudhānaḥ prasitiṃ ta etv ṛtaṃ yo agne anṛtena hanti | tam arciṣā sphūrjayañ jātavedaḥ samakṣam enaṃ gṛṇate ni vṛṅdhi ||
16.7.d: त्रिर् यातुधानः प्रसितिं त एत्व् ऋतं यो अग्ने अनृतेन हन्ति । तम् अर्चिषा स्फूर्जयञ् जातवेदः समक्षम् एनं गृणते नि वृङ्धि ॥
16.7.m: Three times may the sorcerer enter your trap, / he who, O Agni, strikes truth with falsehood! / Thundering with your flame, O Jātavedas, / strike him down before the singer!

16.7.s: yad agne adya mithunā śapāto yad vācas tṛṣṭaṃ janayanta rebhāḥ | manyor manasaḥ śaravyā jāyate yā tayā vidhya hṛdaye yātudhānān ||
16.7.d: यद् अग्ने अद्य मिथुना शपातो यद् वाचस् तृष्टं जनयन्त रेभाः । मन्योर् मनसः शरव्या जायते या तया विध्य हृदये यातुधानान् ॥
16.7.m: If today a pair should curse, O Agni, / if singers have brought forth harsh speech, / whatever missile is born of the mind's fury, / with that pierce the sorcerers in the heart!

16.7.s: parā śṛṇīhi tapasā yātudhānān parāgne rakṣo harasā śṛṇīhi | parārciṣā mūradevāñ chṛṇīhi parāsutṛpaḥ śośucataḥ śṛṇīhi ||
16.7.d: परा शृणीहि तपसा यातुधानान् पराग्ने रक्षो हरसा शृणीहि । परार्चिषा मूरदेवाञ् छृणीहि परासुतृपः शोशुचतः शृणीहि ॥
16.7.m: Crush the sorcerers with your heat; / crush the demon, O Agni, with your fury! / Crush the root-worshiping demons with your flame; / crush the glowing devourers of life-breath!

16.7.s: parādya devā vṛjinaṃ śṛṇantu pratyag enaṃ śapathā yantu sṛṣṭāḥ | vācāstenaṃ śarava ṛcchantu marman viśvayaitu prasitiṃ yātudhānaḥ ||
16.7.d: पराद्य देवा वृजिनं शृणन्तु प्रत्यग् एनं शपथा यन्तु सृष्टाः । वाचास्तेनं शरव ऋच्छन्तु मर्मन् विश्वयैतु प्रसितिं यातुधानः ॥
16.7.m: Today may the gods crush crookedness; / let curses sent forth turn back upon him! / May arrows hit the thief of speech in the vital spot; / may the sorcerer fall into every trap!

16.7.s: sanād agne mṛṇasi yātudhānān na tvā rakṣāṃsi pṛtanāsu jigyuḥ | anu daha sahamūrān kravyādo mā te hetyā mukṣata daivyāyāḥ ||
16.7.d: सनाद् अग्ने मृणसि यातुधानान् न त्वा रक्षांसि पृतनासु जिग्युः । अनु दह सहमूरान् क्रव्यादो मा ते हेत्या मुक्षत दैव्यायाः ॥
16.7.m: From ancient times, O Agni, you crush the sorcerers; / the demons have not conquered you in battles. / Burn down the flesh-eaters together with their roots; / let them not escape your divine weapon!

16.7.s: yaḥ pauruṣeyeṇa kraviṣā samaṅkte yo aśvyena paśunā yātudhānaḥ | yo aghnyāyā bharati kṣīram agne teṣāṃ śīrṣāṇi harasāpi vṛśca ||
16.7.d: यः पौरुषेयेण क्रविषा समङ्क्ते यो अश्व्येन पशुना यातुधानः । यो अघ्न्याया भरति क्षीरम् अग्ने तेषां शीर्षाणि हरसापि वृश्च ॥
16.7.m: The sorcerer who smears himself with human flesh, / who [does so] with horse's or cattle's, / who steals the milk of the unslayable cow, O Agni, / cut off their heads with your fury!

16.7.s: saṃvatsarīṇaṃ paya usriyāyās tasya māsīd yātudhāno nṛcakṣaḥ | pīyūṣam agne yatamas titṛpsāt taṃ pratyañcam arciṣā vidhya marman ||
16.7.d: संवत्सरीणं पय उस्रियायास् तस्य मासीद् यातुधानो नृचक्षः । पीयूषम् अग्ने यतमस् तितृप्सात् तं प्रत्यञ्चम् अर्चिषा विध्य मर्मन् ॥
16.7.m: The yearly milk of the cow— / let not the sorcerer have that, O men-watcher! / Whichever one desires to glut himself on the biestings, O Agni, / pierce him right in the vital spot with your flame as he faces you!

16.7.s: viṣaṃ gavāṃ yātudhānāḥ pibantv ā vṛścantām aditaye durevāḥ | paraiṇān devaḥ savitā dadātu parā bhāgam oṣadhīnāṃ jayantām ||
16.7.d: विषं गवां यातुधानाः पिबन्त्व् आ वृश्चन्ताम् अदितये दुरेवाः । परैणान् देवः सविता ददातु परा भागम् ओषधीनां जयन्ताम् ॥
16.7.m: May the sorcerers drink the poison of cattle; / may the evil-doers be cut off for Aditi! / May the god Savitṛ hand them over; / may they lose their share of the plants!

16.7.s: tvaṃ no agne adharād udaktas tvaṃ paścād uta rakṣā purastāt | prati tye te ajarāsas tapiṣṭhā aghaśaṃsaṃ śośucato dahantu ||
16.7.d: त्वं नो अग्ने अधराद् उदक्तस् त्वं पश्चाद् उत रक्षा पुरस्तात् । प्रति त्ये ते अजरासस् तपिष्ठा अघशंसं शोशुचतो दहन्तु ॥
16.7.m: Do you, O Agni, protect us from below, from above, / do you protect us from behind and from before! / May those hottest, unaging, blazing [flames] of yours / burn the evil-speaker!

16.7.s: paścāt purastād adharād udaktaḥ kaviḥ kāvyena pari pāhy agne | sakhā sakhāyam ajaro jarimṇe agne martyām̐ amartyas tvaṃ naḥ ||
16.7.d: पश्चात् पुरस्ताद् अधराद् उदक्तः कविः काव्येन परि पाह्य् अग्ने । सखा सखायम् अजरो जरिम्णे अग्ने मर्त्याँ अमर्त्यस् त्वं नः ॥
16.7.m: From behind, from before, from below, from above, / as a poet, protect us with your poetic craft, O Agni! / As an unaging friend to a friend for old age, / O immortal Agni, protect us mortals!

16.8.s: tad agne cakṣuḥ prati dhehi rebhe śaphārujaṃ yena paśyasi yātudhānam | atharvavaj jyotiṣā daivyena satyaṃ dhūrvantam acitaṃ ny oṣa ||
16.8.d: तद् अग्ने चक्षुः प्रति धेहि रेभे शफारुजं येन पश्यसि यातुधानम् । अथर्ववज् ज्योतिषा दैव्येन सत्यं धूर्वन्तम् अचितं न्य् ओष ॥
16.8.m: Fix that eye upon the singer, O Agni, / with which you see the hoof-breaking sorcerer; / like Atharvan, with divine light / burn down the senseless one who harms the truth!

16.8.s: pari tvāgne puraṃ vayaṃ vipraṃ sahasya dhīmahi | dhṛṣadvarṇaṃ divedive hantāraṃ bhaṅgurāvatām ||
16.8.d: परि त्वाग्ने पुरं वयं विप्रं सहस्य धीमहि । धृषद्वर्णं दिवेदिवे हन्तारं भङ्गुरावताम् ॥
16.8.m: Around you, O Agni, we set a stronghold, / [around you] the wise, mighty one, / daring in color, day by day / the slayer of deceitful foes.

16.8.s: vi jyotiṣā bṛhatā bhāty agnir āvir viśvāni kṛṇute mahitvā | prādevīr māyāḥ sahate durevāḥ śiśīte śṛṅge rakṣase vinikṣe ||
16.8.d: वि ज्योतिषा बृहता भात्य् अग्निर् आविर् विश्वानि कृणुते महित्वा । प्रादेवीर् मायाः सहते दुरेवाः शिशीते शृङ्गे रक्षसे विनिक्षे ॥
16.8.m: Agni shines forth with great light; / by his greatness he makes all things visible. / He overcomes the ungodly, ill-behaved magic wiles; / he sharpens his two horns to pierce through the rakṣas.

16.8.s: agnī rakṣāṃsi sedhati śukraśocir amartyaḥ | śuciḥ pāvaka īḍyaḥ ||
16.8.d: अग्नी रक्षांसि सेधति शुक्रशोचिर् अमर्त्यः । शुचिः पावक ईड्यः ॥
16.8.m: Agni drives away the rakṣases, / bright-flaming, immortal, / pure, purifying, to be praised.

16.8.s: agne rakṣā ṇo aṃhasaḥ prati ṣma deva rīṣataḥ | tapiṣṭhair ajaro daha ||
16.8.d: अग्ने रक्षा णो अंहसः प्रति ष्म देव रीषतः । तपिष्ठैर् अजरो दह ॥
16.8.m: Protect us, O Agni, from distress, / against the harmer, O god! / Unaging one, burn [them] with your hottest [flames]!

16.8.s: ye te śṛṅge ajare jātavedas tigmaśocī brahmasaṃśite | tābhyāṃ durhārdam abhidāsantaṃ kimīdinaṃ pratyañcaṃ yātudhānaṃ jātavedo vi nikṣva ||
16.8.d: ये ते शृङ्गे अजरे जातवेदस् तिग्मशोची ब्रह्मसंशिते । ताभ्यां दुर्हार्दम् अभिदासन्तं किमीदिनं प्रत्यञ्चं यातुधानं जातवेदो वि निक्ष्व ॥
16.8.m: Those two unaging horns of yours, O Jātavedas, / sharp-flaming, sharpened by sacred formulation— / with them pierce through the ill-hearted Kimīdin who plots against [us], / the sorcerer turning against us, O Jātavedas!

16.8.s: viṣeṇa bhaṅgurāvataḥ sam indra rakṣaso daha | agne śukreṇa śociṣā tapuragrebhir arcibhiḥ ||
16.8.d: विषेण भङ्गुरावतः सम् इन्द्र रक्षसो दह । अग्ने शुक्रेण शोचिषा तपुरग्रेभिर् अर्चिभिः ॥
16.8.m: With poison, O Indra, burn up / the deceitful foes, the rakṣases! / O Agni, with bright flame, / with sparks possessing fiery tips!

16.8.s: praty agne mithunā daha yātudhānā kimīdinā | saṃ tvā śiśāmi jāgṛhy adabdhaṃ vipra manmabhiḥ ||
16.8.d: प्रत्य् अग्ने मिथुना दह यातुधाना किमीदिना । सं त्वा शिशामि जागृह्य् अदब्धं विप्र मन्मभिः ॥
16.8.m: Burn against the couple, O Agni, / the sorcerer and the sorceress Kimīdin! / I sharpen you, be awake; / [I sharpen] the unvanquished, wise one with poetic thoughts.

16.8.s: praty agne harasā haraḥ śṛṇīhi viśvataḥ prati | yātudhānasya rakṣaso balaṃ vi ruja vīryam ||
16.8.d: प्रत्य् अग्ने हरसा हरः शृणीहि विश्वतः प्रति । यातुधानस्य रक्षसो बलं वि रुज वीर्यम् ॥
16.8.m: With heat strike against heat, O Agni; / crush [it] from every side! / Shatter the strength, the prowess / of the sorcerer, of the rakṣas!

16.8.s: sādānveyaṃ pra mṛṇa rakṣa indra yātudhānakṣayaṇair mūraiḥ | etāv agne mithunā yātudhānā viṣvañcau mruktau harasā śayātām ||
16.8.d: सादान्वेयं प्र मृण रक्ष इन्द्र यातुधानक्षयणैर् मूरैः । एताव् अग्ने मिथुना यातुधाना विष्वञ्चौ म्रुक्तौ हरसा शयाताम् ॥
16.8.m: Crush Sādānva's kin, the rakṣas, O Indra, / with fools who destroy sorcerers! / Let this couple, the two sorcerers, O Agni, / lie scattered apart by your heat!

16.8.s: bṛhaspatir naḥ pari pātu paścād utottarasmād adharād aghāyoḥ | indraḥ purastād uta madhyato naḥ sakhā sakhibhyo varīyaḥ kṛṇotu ||
16.8.d: बृहस्पतिर् नः परि पातु पश्चाद् उतोत्तरस्माद् अधराद् अघायोः । इन्द्रः पुरस्ताद् उत मध्यतो नः सखा सखिभ्यो वरीयः कृणोतु ॥
16.8.m: May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind, / and from above, and from below against the malevolent! / May Indra from the front and from the middle / make wide space for us, a friend for his friends!

16.9.s: indrāsomā tapataṃ rakṣa ubjataṃ ny arpayataṃ vṛṣaṇā tamovṛdhaḥ | parā śṛṇīhi tam acito ny oṣataṃ hataṃ nudethāṃ ni śiśītam atriṇaḥ ||
16.9.d: इन्द्रासोमा तपतं रक्ष उब्जतं न्य् अर्पयतं वृषणा तमोवृधः । परा शृणीहि तम् अचितो न्य् ओषतं हतं नुदेथां नि शिशीतम् अत्रिणः ॥
16.9.m: O Indra and Soma, torment the rakṣas, subdue [it]; / cast down, O manly ones, those who thrive in darkness! / Smash that senseless one away, burn [them] down; / slay, thrust away, crush the rapacious [demons]!

16.9.s: indrāsomā sam aghaśaṃsam abhy aghaṃ tapur yayastu carur agnivām̐ iva | brahmadviṣe kravyāde ghoracakṣase dveṣo dhattam anavāyaṃ kimīdine ||
16.9.d: इन्द्रासोमा सम् अघशंसम् अभ्य् अघं तपुर् ययस्तु चरुर् अग्निवाँ इव । ब्रह्मद्विषे क्रव्यादे घोरचक्षसे द्वेषो धत्तम् अनवायं किमीदिने ॥
16.9.m: O Indra and Soma, let hot torment boil against the evil-plotter / like a vessel with fire! / Against the hater of sacred formulations, the raw-flesh eater, the dread-eyed one, / the Kimīdin, set unending hatred!

16.9.s: indrāsomā duṣkṛto vavre antar anārambhaṇe tamasi pra vidhyatam | yathaiṣāṃ nātaḥ punar ekaś canodayat tad vām astu sahase manyumac chavaḥ ||
16.9.d: इन्द्रासोमा दुष्कृतो वव्रे अन्तर् अनारम्भणे तमसि प्र विध्यतम् । यथैषां नातः पुनर् एकश् चनोदयत् तद् वाम् अस्तु सहसे मन्युमच् छवः ॥
16.9.m: O Indra and Soma, pierce the wrongdoers down into the chasm, / into darkness having no foothold! / So that not even one of them shall ever rise again from there; / let that be your furious strength for victory!

16.9.s: indrāsomā vartayataṃ divas pary agnitaptebhir yuvam aśmahanmabhiḥ | tapurvadhebhir ajarebhir atriṇo ni parśāne vidhyataṃ yantu nisvaram ||
16.9.d: इन्द्रासोमा वर्तयतं दिवस् पर्य् अग्नितप्तेभिर् युवम् अश्महन्मभिः । तपुर्वधेभिर् अजरेभिर् अत्रिणो नि पर्शाने विध्यतं यन्तु निस्वरम् ॥
16.9.m: O Indra and Soma, roll from the sky / with your stone-smiting [bolts] heated by fire; / with your unaging missiles of fiery death, / pierce the rapacious down into the ravine; let them go soundless!

16.9.s: indrāsomā pra harataṃ divo vadhaṃ saṃ pṛthivyā aghaśaṃsāya tarhaṇam | ut takṣataṃ svaryaṃ parvatebhyo yena rakṣo vavṛdhānaṃ nijūrvathaḥ ||
16.9.d: इन्द्रासोमा प्र हरतं दिवो वधं सं पृथिव्या अघशंसाय तर्हणम् । उत् तक्षतं स्वर्यं पर्वतेभ्यो येन रक्षो ववृधानं निजूर्वथः ॥
16.9.m: O Indra and Soma, launch the weapon from heaven, / smashing together from the earth against the evil-plotter! / Fashion from the mountains the heavenly [weapon] / with which you burn down the grown rakṣas!

16.9.s: indrāsomā pari vāṃ bhūtu viśvata iyaṃ matiḥ kakṣyāśveva vājinā | yāṃ vāṃ hotrāṃ pari hiṇomi medhayā imā brahmāṇi nṛpatīva jinvatam ||
16.9.d: इन्द्रासोमा परि वां भूतु विश्वत इयं मतिः कक्ष्याश्वेव वाजिना । यां वां होत्रां परि हिणोमि मेधया इमा ब्रह्माणि नृपतीव जिन्वतम् ॥
16.9.m: O Indra and Soma, let this prayer encompass you from all sides, / like a girth around two swift horses, / the invocation which I send forth to you with wisdom— / like two lords of men, quicken these sacred formulations!

16.9.s: prati smarethāṃ tujayadbhir evair hataṃ druho rakṣaso bhaṅgurāvataḥ | indrāsomā duṣkṛte mā sugaṃ bhūd yo mā kadā cid abhidāsati druhuḥ ||
16.9.d: प्रति स्मरेथां तुजयद्भिर् एवैर् हतं द्रुहो रक्षसो भङ्गुरावतः । इन्द्रासोमा दुष्कृते मा सुगं भूद् यो मा कदा चिद् अभिदासति द्रुहुः ॥
16.9.m: Take heed with rushing advances; / slay the treacherous deceitful foes, the rakṣases! / O Indra and Soma, let there be no easy going for the evildoer, / the deceitful one who plots against me at any time!

16.9.s: yo mā pākena manasā carantam abhicaṣṭe anṛtebhir vacobhiḥ | āpa iva kāśinā saṃgṛbhītā asann astv asata indra vaktā ||
16.9.d: यो मा पाकेन मनसा चरन्तम् अभिचष्टे अनृतेभिर् वचोभिः । आप इव काशिना संगृभीता असन्न् अस्त्व् असत इन्द्र वक्ता ॥
16.9.m: He who looks upon me as I walk with simple mind / with untrue words, / like waters grasped in the fist, / let that speaker of falsehood, O Indra, be non-existent!

16.9.s: ye pākaśaṃsaṃ viharanta evair ye vā bhadraṃ dūṣayanti svadhābhiḥ | ahaye vā tān pradadātu soma ā vā dadhātu nirṛter upasthe ||
16.9.d: ये पाकशंसं विहरन्त एवैर् ये वा भद्रं दूषयन्ति स्वधाभिः । अहये वा तान् प्रददातु सोम आ वा दधातु निरृतेर् उपस्थे ॥
16.9.m: Those who break apart the simple-minded utterance with their ways, / or who corrupt what is good by their customary habits— / may Soma hand them over to the serpent, / or place them into the lap of Nirṛti!

16.9.s: yo no rasaṃ dipsati pitvo agne yo aśvānāṃ yo gavāṃ yas tanūnām | ripu stena steyakṛd dabhram etu ni ṣa hīyatāṃ tanvā tanā ca ||
16.9.d: यो नो रसं दिप्सति पित्वो अग्ने यो अश्वानां यो गवां यस् तनूनाम् । रिपु स्तेन स्तेयकृद् दभ्रम् एतु नि ष हीयतां तन्वा तना च ॥
16.9.m: He who seeks to harm the essence of our nourishment, O Agni, / who [seeks to harm] that of our horses, of our cows, of our bodies— / let that hostile one, a thief, a committer of theft, come to nothing; / let him be ruined in body and in offspring!

16.10.s: paraḥ so astu tanvā tanā ca tisraḥ pṛthivīr adho astu viśvāḥ | prati śuṣyati yaśo asya devā yo mā divā dipsati yaś ca naktam ||
16.10.d: परः सो अस्तु तन्वा तना च तिस्रः पृथिवीर् अधो अस्तु विश्वाः । प्रति शुष्यति यशो अस्य देवा यो मा दिवा दिप्सति यश् च नक्तम् ॥
16.10.m: Let him be far off in body and in offspring; / let him be below all three earths! / O gods, may the fame of him dry up, / whoever seeks to harm me by day and whoever by night!

16.10.s: suvijñānaṃ cikituṣe janāya sac cāsac ca vacasī paspṛśāte | tayor yat satyaṃ yatarad ṛjīyas tad it somo 'vati hanty āsat ||
16.10.d: सुविज्ञानं चिकितुषे जनाय सच् चासच् च वचसी पस्पृशाते । तयोर् यत् सत्यं यतरद् ऋजीयस् तद् इत् सोमो ऽवति हन्त्य् आसत् ॥
16.10.m: Easy to discern for a discerning person / are the two words, true and untrue, as they clash; / of the two, that which is true, whichever is more upright, / that Soma favors; he smites the untrue.

16.10.s: na vā u somo vṛjinaṃ hinoti na kṣatriyaṃ mithuyā dhārayantam | hanti rakṣo hanty āsad vadantam ubhāv indrasya prasitau śayāte ||
16.10.d: न वा उ सोमो वृजिनं हिनोति न क्षत्रियं मिथुया धारयन्तम् । हन्ति रक्षो हन्त्य् आसद् वदन्तम् उभाव् इन्द्रस्य प्रसितौ शयाते ॥
16.10.m: Soma does not further the crooked person, / nor the ruler who maintains false ways; / he slays the rakṣas, he slays the one speaking untruth; / both lie in the snare of Indra.

16.10.s: yadi vāham anṛtadevo asmi moghaṃ vā devām̐ apyūhe agne | kim asmabhyaṃ jātavedo hṛṇīṣe droghavācas te nirṛthaṃ sacantām ||
16.10.d: यदि वाहम् अनृतदेवो अस्मि मोघं वा देवाँ अप्यूहे अग्ने । किम् अस्मभ्यं जातवेदो हृणीषे द्रोघवाचस् ते निरृथं सचन्ताम् ॥
16.10.m: If I am one whose gods are false, / or if I have had vain thoughts about the gods, O Agni— / why are you angry at us, O Jātavedas? / Let those of deceptive speech meet with destruction!

16.10.s: adyā murīya yadi yātudhāno asmi yadi vāyus tatapa pūruṣasya | adhā sa vīrair daśabhir vi yūyā yo mā moghaṃ yātudhānety aha ||
16.10.d: अद्या मुरीय यदि यातुधानो अस्मि यदि वायुस् ततप पूरुषस्य । अधा स वीरैर् दशभिर् वि यूया यो मा मोघं यातुधानेत्य् अह ॥
16.10.m: May I die today if I am a sorcerer, / or if I [have scorched] the life of a man! / But may he be separated from ten sons, / who vainly says to me, 'O sorcerer!'

16.10.s: yo māyātuṃ yātudhānety āha yo mā rakṣāḥ śucir asmīty āha | indras taṃ hantu mahatā vadhena viśvasya jantor adhamas padīṣṭa ||
16.10.d: यो मायातुं यातुधानेत्य् आह यो मा रक्षाः शुचिर् अस्मीत्य् आह । इन्द्रस् तं हन्तु महता वधेन विश्वस्य जन्तोर् अधमस् पदीष्ट ॥
16.10.m: He who calls me a sorcerer when I am no sorcerer, / or who, being a rakṣas, says 'I am pure'— / let Indra slay him with a great weapon; / let him fall lowest of all creatures!

16.10.s: pra yā jigāti khargaleva naktam apa druhus tanvaṃ gūhamānā | vavrām̐ anantām̐ ava sā padīṣṭa grāvāṇo ghnantu rakṣasa upabdaiḥ ||
16.10.d: प्र या जिगाति खर्गलेव नक्तम् अप द्रुहुस् तन्वं गूहमाना । वव्राँ अनन्ताँ अव सा पदीष्ट ग्रावाणो घ्नन्तु रक्षस उपब्दैः ॥
16.10.m: She who stalks by night like an owl, / the treacherous one hiding her body— / may she fall down into endless pits; / let the pressing-stones crush the rakṣases with their rumblings!

16.10.s: vi tiṣṭhadhvaṃ maruto vikṣv icchata gṛbhāyata rakṣasaḥ saṃ pinaṣṭana | vayo ye bhūtvā patayanti naktabhir ye vā ripo dadhire deve adhvare ||
16.10.d: वि तिष्ठध्वं मरुतो विक्ष्व् इच्छत गृभायत रक्षसः सं पिनष्टन । वयो ये भूत्वा पतयन्ति नक्तभिर् ये वा रिपो दधिरे देवे अध्वरे ॥
16.10.m: Disperse among the clans, O Maruts; / seize the rakṣases, grind them to pieces! / Those who, having become birds, fly about by night, / or who have placed hostilities at the divine rite!

16.10.s: eta u tye patayanti śvayātava indraṃ dipsanti dipsavo 'dābhyam | śiśīte śakraḥ piśunebhyo vadhaṃ nūnaṃ sṛjad aśaniṃ yātumadbhyaḥ ||
16.10.d: एत उ त्ये पतयन्ति श्वयातव इन्द्रं दिप्सन्ति दिप्सवो ऽदाभ्यम् । शिशीते शक्रः पिशुनेभ्यो वधं नूनं सृजद् अशनिं यातुमद्भ्यः ॥
16.10.m: Here fly those dog-sorcerers; / seeking to harm, they seek to harm Indra, who cannot be harmed. / The mighty one sharpens his weapon for the slanderers; / now he will hurl his thunderbolt against the sorcerers.

16.10.s: pra vartaya divo aśmānam indra somaśitaṃ maghavan saṃ śiśādhi | prākto apākto adharād udakto abhi jahi rakṣasaḥ parvatena ||
16.10.d: प्र वर्तय दिवो अश्मानम् इन्द्र सोमशितं मघवन् सं शिशाधि । प्राक्तो अपाक्तो अधराद् उदक्तो अभि जहि रक्षसः पर्वतेन ॥
16.10.m: Roll down the stone from heaven, / O Indra; O bounteous one, sharpen [it] whetted by Soma! / From the east, from the west, from below, from above, / strike down the rakṣases with the mountain-rock!

16.11.s: indro yātūnām abhavat parāśaro havirmathīnām abhy āvivāsatām | abhīd u śakraḥ paraśur yathā vanaṃ pātreva bhindant sata eti rakṣasaḥ ||
16.11.d: इन्द्रो यातूनाम् अभवत् पराशरो हविर्मथीनाम् अभ्य् आविवासताम् । अभीद् उ शक्रः परशुर् यथा वनं पात्रेव भिन्दन्त् सत एति रक्षसः ॥
16.11.m: Indra became the destroyer of the sorcerers / who strive to approach and ruin the oblations; / the mighty one goes forth splitting the rakṣases / as an axe [splits] a forest, as [one breaks] pots.

16.11.s: ulūkayātuṃ śuśulūkayātuṃ jahi śvayātum uta kokayātum | suparṇayātum uta gṛdhrayātuṃ dṛṣadeva pra mṛṇa rakṣa indra ||
16.11.d: उलूकयातुं शुशुलूकयातुं जहि श्वयातुम् उत कोकयातुम् । सुपर्णयातुम् उत गृध्रयातुं दृषदेव प्र मृण रक्ष इन्द्र ॥
16.11.m: The owl-sorcerer, the owlet-sorcerer, / slay the dog-sorcerer and the cuckoo-sorcerer! / The eagle-sorcerer and the vulture-sorcerer, / crush the rakṣas, O Indra, like a millstone!

16.11.s: mā no rakṣo abhi naḍ yātumāvatām apocchataṃ mithunā yā kimīdinā | pṛthivī naḥ pārthivāt pātv aṃhaso antarikṣaṃ divyāt pātv asmān ||
16.11.d: मा नो रक्षो अभि नड् यातुमावताम् अपोच्छतं मिथुना या किमीदिना । पृथिवी नः पार्थिवात् पात्व् अंहसो अन्तरिक्षं दिव्यात् पात्व् अस्मान् ॥
16.11.m: Let not the rakṣas of the sorcerers reach us; / let the two Kimīdin couples depart! / May the earth protect us from earthly distress; / may the intermediate space protect us from heavenly [distress]!

16.11.s: indra jahi pumāṃsaṃ yātudhānam uta striyaṃ māyayā śāśadānām | vigrīvāso mūradevā rudantu mā te dṛśan sūryam uccarantam ||
16.11.d: इन्द्र जहि पुमांसं यातुधानम् उत स्त्रियं मायया शाशदानाम् । विग्रीवासो मूरदेवा रुदन्तु मा ते दृशन् सूर्यम् उच्चरन्तम् ॥
16.11.m: O Indra, slay the male sorcerer, / and the woman exulting in sorcery! / Let the fool-gods howl with broken necks; / may they not see the rising sun!

16.11.s: prati cakṣva vi cakṣva indraś ca soma jāgṛtam | rakṣobhyo vadham asyatam aśaniṃ yātumadbhyaḥ ||
16.11.d: प्रति चक्ष्व वि चक्ष्व इन्द्रश् च सोम जागृतम् । रक्षोभ्यो वधम् अस्यतम् अशनिं यातुमद्भ्यः ॥
16.11.m: Look out, look around, / and be watchful, O Indra and Soma! / Hurl your weapon at the rakṣases, / your thunderbolt against the sorcerers!

16.12.s: yā babhravo yāś ca śukrā rohiṇīr uta pṛśnayaḥ | asiknīḥ kṛṣṇā oṣadhīḥ sarvā acchā vadāmasi ||
16.12.d: या बभ्रवो याश् च शुक्रा रोहिणीर् उत पृश्नयः । असिक्नीः कृष्णा ओषधीः सर्वा अच्छा वदामसि ॥
16.12.m: Those that are brown and those that are bright, / red and dappled, / the dark and black herbs— / we address them all.

16.12.s: trāyantām imaṃ puruṣaṃ yakṣmād deveṣitād adhi | yāsāṃ dyauṣ pitā pṛthivī mātā samudro mūlaṃ vīrudhāṃ babhūva ||
16.12.d: त्रायन्ताम् इमं पुरुषं यक्ष्माद् देवेषिताद् अधि । यासां द्यौष् पिता पृथिवी माता समुद्रो मूलं वीरुधां बभूव ॥
16.12.m: May they rescue this man / from the consumption sent by the gods— / they whose father was heaven, whose mother was earth, / whose root was the ocean, the plants!

16.12.s: āpo 'graṃ divyā oṣadhayas | tās te yakṣmam enasyam aṅgādaṅgād anīnaśan ||
16.12.d: आपो ऽग्रं दिव्या ओषधयस् । तास् ते यक्ष्मम् एनस्यम् अङ्गादङ्गाद् अनीनशन् ॥
16.12.m: Waters are the foremost divine plants; / let them banish from limb to limb / your consumption born of sin.

16.12.s: prastṛṇatī stambinīr ekaśṛṅgāḥ pratanvatīr oṣadhīr ā vadāmi | aṃśumatīḥ kāṇḍinīr yā viśākhā hvayāmi te vīrudho vaiśvadevīr ugrāḥ puruṣajīvanīḥ ||
16.12.d: प्रस्तृणती स्तम्बिनीर् एकशृङ्गाः प्रतन्वतीर् ओषधीर् आ वदामि । अंशुमतीः काण्डिनीर् या विशाखा ह्वयामि ते वीरुधो वैश्वदेवीर् उग्राः पुरुषजीवनीः ॥
16.12.m: Spreading, bushy, single-pointed, / extending herbs I address; / shoot-bearing, jointed, branching— / I invoke for you the plants belonging to all the gods, / fierce, giving life to man.

16.12.s: yad vaḥ sahaḥ sahamānā vīryaṃ yac ca vo balam | tenemam asmād yakṣmāt puruṣaṃ muñcantauṣadhīḥ ||
16.12.d: यद् वः सहः सहमाना वीर्यं यच् च वो बलम् । तेनेमम् अस्माद् यक्ष्मात् पुरुषं मुञ्चन्तौषधीः ॥
16.12.m: What overcoming power is yours, / what vigor, and what strength— / with that release this man / from this consumption, O herbs!

16.12.s: jīvalāṃ naghāriṣāṃ jīvantīm oṣadhīm uta | arundhatīm unnayantīṃ puṣpāṃ madhumatīṃ huve ||
16.12.d: जीवलां नघारिषां जीवन्तीम् ओषधीम् उत । अरुन्धतीम् उन्नयन्तीं पुष्पां मधुमतीं हुवे ॥
16.12.m: The live-giving, the harm-averting, / and the living herb, / the wound-healing, the uplifting, / the blossoming, the rich in honey I call.

16.12.s: ihā yantu pracetaso medinīr vacaso mama | yathemaṃ pārayāmasi puruṣaṃ duritād adhi ||
16.12.d: इहा यन्तु प्रचेतसो मेदिनीर् वचसो मम । यथेमं पारयामसि पुरुषं दुरिताद् अधि ॥
16.12.m: Let them come hither, wise, / friendly to my speech, / so that we may ferry this man / across misfortune.

16.12.s: agner ghāso apāṃ garbho yā rohanti punarṇavāḥ | dhruvāḥ sahasranāmnīr bheṣajīḥ santv ābhṛtāḥ ||
16.12.d: अग्नेर् घासो अपां गर्भो या रोहन्ति पुनर्णवाः । ध्रुवाः सहस्रनाम्नीर् भेषजीः सन्त्व् आभृताः ॥
16.12.m: Fodder of Agni, embryo of the waters, / which grow ever anew, / steadfast, thousand-named, / brought hither let them be remedies.

16.12.s: avakolvā udakātmāna oṣadhayaḥ | vyajṛṣantī duritaṃ tīkṣṇaśṛṅgyaḥ ||
16.12.d: अवकोल्वा उदकात्मान ओषधयः । व्यजृषन्ती दुरितं तीक्ष्णशृङ्ग्यः ॥
16.12.m: Having the avakā-reed for womb, whose self is water, the herbs; / sharp-horned, they crush away misfortune.

16.12.s: unmuñcantīr vivaruṇā ugrā yā viṣadūṣanīr atho balāsanāśanīḥ | rakṣonāśanīḥ kṛtyādūṣaṇīś ca yās tā ihā yantv oṣadhīḥ ||
16.12.d: उन्मुञ्चन्तीर् विवरुणा उग्रा या विषदूषनीर् अथो बलासनाशनीः । रक्षोनाशनीः कृत्यादूषणीश् च यास् ता इहा यन्त्व् ओषधीः ॥
16.12.m: Untying [fetters], free from Varuṇa, / fierce, which are poison-spoilers, / and also balāsa-destroyers; / destroyers of rakṣases, and spoilers of sorcery— / let those herbs come hither.

16.13.s: śivās te santv oṣadhīr apakrītāḥ sahīyasīr vīrudho yā abhiṣṭutāḥ | apāṃ sarasvatīṃ jyeṣṭhāṃ trāyantām asmākaṃ gām aśvaṃ puruṣaṃ paśum ||
16.13.d: शिवास् ते सन्त्व् ओषधीर् अपक्रीताः सहीयसीर् वीरुधो या अभिष्टुताः । अपां सरस्वतीं ज्येष्ठां त्रायन्ताम् अस्माकं गाम् अश्वं पुरुषं पशुम् ॥
16.13.m: Auspicious to you be the herbs when bought, / most powerful the plants that are praised; / may the eldest Sarasvatī of the waters protect / our cow, horse, man, and beast.

16.13.s: madhuman mūlaṃ madhumad agram āsāṃ madhuman madhyaṃ vīrudhāṃ babhūva | madhumat parṇaṃ madhumat puṣpam āsāṃ madhoḥ saṃbhūtā amṛtasya bhakṣo ghṛtam annaṃ duhrate gopurogavam ||
16.13.d: मधुमन् मूलं मधुमद् अग्रम् आसां मधुमन् मध्यं वीरुधां बभूव । मधुमत् पर्णं मधुमत् पुष्पम् आसां मधोः संभूता अमृतस्य भक्षो घृतम् अन्नं दुह्रते गोपुरोगवम् ॥
16.13.m: Sweet is their root, sweet their tip, / sweet was the middle of these plants; / sweet is their leaf, sweet their blossom; / sprung from sweetness, food of nectar, / they yield ghee and food, preceded by the cow.

16.13.s: yāvatīḥ kīyatīś cemāḥ pṛthivyām adhy oṣadhīḥ | tā naḥ sahasraparṇyo mṛtyor muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
16.13.d: यावतीः कीयतीश् चेमाः पृथिव्याम् अध्य् ओषधीः । ता नः सहस्रपर्ण्यो मृत्योर् मुञ्चन्त्व् अंहसः ॥
16.13.m: As many and however many / these herbs are upon the earth, / let them, thousand-leaved, / release us from death and distress.

16.13.s: vaiyāghro maṇir vīrudhāṃ trāyamāṇo 'bhiśastipāḥ | amīvāḥ sarvā rakṣāṃsy apa hantv adhi dūram asmat ||
16.13.d: वैयाघ्रो मणिर् वीरुधां त्रायमाणो ऽभिशस्तिपाः । अमीवाः सर्वा रक्षांस्य् अप हन्त्व् अधि दूरम् अस्मत् ॥
16.13.m: The tiger-amulet among the plants, / protecting, warding off curses, / let it strike away all diseases, / the rakṣases far away from us.

16.13.s: siṃhasyeva stanathor oṣadhīnām agner iva vijanta ābhṛtābhyaḥ | gavāṃ yakṣmaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ vīrudbhir atinutto nāvyā etu srotyāḥ ||
16.13.d: सिंहस्येव स्तनथोर् ओषधीनाम् अग्नेर् इव विजन्त आभृताभ्यः । गवां यक्ष्मः पुरुषाणां वीरुद्भिर् अतिनुत्तो नाव्या एतु स्रोत्याः ॥
16.13.m: As from the roar of a lion, as from fire, / they flee trembling from the brought herbs; / the consumption of cows and men / is driven by the plants across the navigable streams.

16.13.s: mumucānā oṣadhayo agner vaiśvānarād adhi | bhūmiṃ saṃtanvatīr ita yāsāṃ rājā vanaspatiḥ ||
16.13.d: मुमुचाना ओषधयो अग्नेर् वैश्वानराद् अधि । भूमिं संतन्वतीर् इत यासां राजा वनस्पतिः ॥
16.13.m: Released, O herbs, / from Agni Vaiśvānara, / go overspreading the earth, / you whose king is the tree.

16.13.s: yāś cāhaṃ veda vīrudho yāś ca paśyāmi cakṣuṣā | ajñātā jānīmaś ca yā yāsu vidmasi saṃbhṛtam | sarvāḥ samagrā oṣadhīr bodhantu vacaso mama ||
16.13.d: याश् चाहं वेद वीरुधो याश् च पश्यामि चक्षुषा । अज्ञाता जानीमश् च या यासु विद्मसि संभृतम् । सर्वाः समग्रा ओषधीर् बोधन्तु वचसो मम ॥
16.13.m: Which plants I know, / and which I see with the eye, / the unknown and those that we know, / in which we know [power] is gathered— / let all herbs together / take heed of my speech.

16.13.s: yā rohanty āṅgirasīḥ parvateṣu sameṣu ca vīrudho viśvabheṣajīḥ | tā no mayasvatīḥ śivā oṣadhīḥ santu śaṃ hṛde ||
16.13.d: या रोहन्त्य् आङ्गिरसीः पर्वतेषु समेषु च वीरुधो विश्वभेषजीः । ता नो मयस्वतीः शिवा ओषधीः सन्तु शं हृदे ॥
16.13.m: Those belonging to the Aṅgirases that grow / on mountains and in plains, / the plants of all healing— / may they be delightful and auspicious to us, / herbs bringing bliss to the heart.

16.13.s: aśvattho darbho vīrudhāṃ somo rājāmṛtaṃ haviḥ | vrīhir yavaś ca bheṣajau divas putrāv amartyau ||
16.13.d: अश्वत्थो दर्भो वीरुधां सोमो राजामृतं हविः । व्रीहिर् यवश् च भेषजौ दिवस् पुत्राव् अमर्त्यौ ॥
16.13.m: Aśvattha, darbha-grass among plants, / king Soma, the nectar-oblation; / rice and barley, the two healing, / immortal sons of heaven.

16.13.s: uj jīhīdhve stanayaty abhikrandanty oṣadhīḥ | yadā vaḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ parjanyo retasāvati ||
16.13.d: उज् जीहीध्वे स्तनयत्य् अभिक्रन्दन्त्य् ओषधीः । यदा वः पृश्निमातरः पर्जन्यो रेतसावति ॥
16.13.m: You rise up, when it thunders, / herbs greeting it with shouts, / when Parjanya, O you whose mother is Pṛśni, / favors you with seed.

16.14.s: tasyāmṛtasyemaṃ balaṃ puruṣaṃ pārayāmasi | atho kṛṇomi bheṣajaṃ yathāsac chatahāyanaḥ ||
16.14.d: तस्यामृतस्येमं बलं पुरुषं पारयामसि । अथो कृणोमि भेषजं यथासच् छतहायनः ॥
16.14.m: With the power of that nectar / we ferry this man across; / and I make a remedy, / that he may live a hundred years.

16.14.s: varāho veda vīrudhaṃ nakulo veda bheṣajīḥ | gandharvāḥ sarpā yā vidus tā ihā yantv oṣadhīḥ ||
16.14.d: वराहो वेद वीरुधं नकुलो वेद भेषजीः । गन्धर्वाः सर्पा या विदुस् ता इहा यन्त्व् ओषधीः ॥
16.14.m: The boar knows the plant; / the mongoose knows the healing herbs; / what the Gandharvas and serpents know— / let those herbs come hither.

16.14.s: yāḥ suparṇā āṅgirasīr divyā yā raghaṭo viduḥ | vayāṃsi haṃsā yā vidur yāś ca sarve patatriṇaḥ | mṛgā yā vidur oṣadhīs tā asmā avase huve ||
16.14.d: याः सुपर्णा आङ्गिरसीर् दिव्या या रघटो विदुः । वयांसि हंसा या विदुर् याश् च सर्वे पतत्रिणः । मृगा या विदुर् ओषधीस् ता अस्मा अवसे हुवे ॥
16.14.m: Which Aṅgiras-plants the eagles know, / the divine ones which the raghaṭas know, / which the birds and swans know, / and which all winged creatures know, / the herbs which beasts know, / those I call to his aid.

16.14.s: yāvatīnām oṣadhīnāṃ gāvaḥ prāśnanty aghnyā yāvatīnām ajāvayaḥ | tāvatīr viśvabheṣajīr ā bharāmi tvām abhi ||
16.14.d: यावतीनाम् ओषधीनां गावः प्राश्नन्त्य् अघ्न्या यावतीनाम् अजावयः । तावतीर् विश्वभेषजीर् आ भरामि त्वाम् अभि ॥
16.14.m: As many herbs as / the cows, the inviolable, eat, / as many as the goats and sheep— / so many all-healing herbs / I bring to you.

16.14.s: yāvatīṣu manuṣyā bheṣajaṃ bhiṣajo viduḥ | tāvatīs tubhyam ābhṛtāḥ śarma yacchantv oṣadhīḥ ||
16.14.d: यावतीषु मनुष्या भेषजं भिषजो विदुः । तावतीस् तुभ्यम् आभृताः शर्म यच्छन्त्व् ओषधीः ॥
16.14.m: In as many [herbs] as men / and physicians know healing— / so many, brought for you, / let the herbs grant protection.

16.14.s: puṣpavatīḥ prasūmatīḥ phalinīr aphalā uta | saṃmātara iva duhrām asmā ariṣṭatātaye ||
16.14.d: पुष्पवतीः प्रसूमतीः फलिनीर् अफला उत । संमातर इव दुह्राम् अस्मा अरिष्टतातये ॥
16.14.m: Blossoming, sprouting, / fruit-bearing and fruitless, / like mothers together let them yield [bounty] / for this man's unharmed condition.

16.14.s: ut tvāhārṣaṃ pañcaśalād ut tvā daśaśalād uta | ut tvā yamasya paḍvīśād oṣadhībhir apīparam ||
16.14.d: उत् त्वाहार्षं पञ्चशलाद् उत् त्वा दशशलाद् उत । उत् त्वा यमस्य पड्वीशाद् ओषधीभिर् अपीपरम् ॥
16.14.m: I have pulled you up from a five-pronged [fetter], / and from a ten-pronged one I have pulled you up; / up from Yama's fetter / I have ferried you across with herbs.

16.15.s: indrasya prathamo ratho devānām aparo ratho varuṇasya tṛtīya it | ahīnām apamā ratha sthāṇum ārad athā riṣat ||
16.15.d: इन्द्रस्य प्रथमो रथो देवानाम् अपरो रथो वरुणस्य तृतीय इत् । अहीनाम् अपमा रथ स्थाणुम् आरद् अथा रिषत् ॥
16.15.m: Indra's is the first chariot, / the other chariot belongs to the gods, / Varuṇa's is the third; / the chariot of the serpents is the hindmost: / it struck a post and then came to grief.

16.15.s: darbhaḥ śocis tarūṇakam aśvasya vāraḥ puruṣasya vāraḥ | rathasya bandhuram ahīnām arasaṃ viṣaṃ vār id ugram ||
16.15.d: दर्भः शोचिस् तरूणकम् अश्वस्य वारः पुरुषस्य वारः । रथस्य बन्धुरम् अहीनाम् अरसं विषं वार् इद् उग्रम् ॥
16.15.m: The darbha-grass, the flame, the young shoot, / the horse's tail-hair, the man's hair, / the chariot's […]; / the sapless poison of the serpents is just fierce water.

16.15.s: ava śveta padā jahi pūrveṇa cāpareṇa ca | udaplutam iva dārv ahīnām arasaṃ viṣaṃ vār id ugram ||
16.15.d: अव श्वेत पदा जहि पूर्वेण चापरेण च । उदप्लुतम् इव दार्व् अहीनाम् अरसं विषं वार् इद् उग्रम् ॥
16.15.m: Strike down with the foot, O white one, / with the fore-[foot] and the hind-[foot]! / Like wood floating on water, / the sapless poison of the serpents is just fierce water.

16.15.s: araṃghaso nimajya unmajya punar abravīt | udaplutam iva dārv ahīnām arasaṃ viṣaṃ vār id ugram ||
16.15.d: अरंघसो निमज्य उन्मज्य पुनर् अब्रवीत् । उदप्लुतम् इव दार्व् अहीनाम् अरसं विषं वार् इद् उग्रम् ॥
16.15.m: Swiftly diving, / emerging, he spoke again: / like wood floating on water, / the sapless poison of the serpents is just fierce water.

16.15.s: paidvo hanti kaṣarṇīlaṃ paidvaḥ śvitram utāsitam | paidvo ratharvyāḥ śiraḥ saṃ bibheda pṛdākvāḥ ||
16.15.d: पैद्वो हन्ति कषर्णीलं पैद्वः श्वित्रम् उतासितम् । पैद्वो रथर्व्याः शिरः सं बिभेद पृदाक्वाः ॥
16.15.m: The paidva-steed kills the kasarṇīla, / the white [snake] and the black; / the paidva has cleft the head / of the ratharvī-viper, the adder.

16.15.s: paidva prehi prathamo anu tvā vayam emasi | ahīn vy asyatāt patho yena smā vayam emasi ||
16.15.d: पैद्व प्रेहि प्रथमो अनु त्वा वयम् एमसि । अहीन् व्य् अस्यतात् पथो येन स्मा वयम् एमसि ॥
16.15.m: O paidva-steed, go first; / we follow after you; / cast the serpents from the path / along which we are going!

16.15.s: idaṃ paidvo ajāyata idam asya parāyaṇam | imāny arvataḥ padā ahighnyo vājinīvataḥ ||
16.15.d: इदं पैद्वो अजायत इदम् अस्य परायणम् । इमान्य् अर्वतः पदा अहिघ्न्यो वाजिनीवतः ॥
16.15.m: Here the paidva-steed was born; / this is his departure; / these are the tracks of the courser, / the slayer of serpents, rich in mares.

16.15.s: saṃyataṃ na vi ṣparad vyāttaṃ na saṃ yamat | asmin kṣetre dvāv ahī strī ca pumāṃś ca tā ubhā arasā ||
16.15.d: संयतं न वि ष्परद् व्यात्तं न सं यमत् । अस्मिन् क्षेत्रे द्वाव् अही स्त्री च पुमांश् च ता उभा अरसा ॥
16.15.m: Let it not open wide what is shut; / let it not shut what is opened wide; / in this field are two serpents, / female and male, both of them sapless.

16.15.s: arasāsa ihāhayo ye anti ye ca dūrake | ghanena hanmi vṛścikam ahiṃ daṇḍenāgatam ||
16.15.d: अरसास इहाहयो ये अन्ति ये च दूरके । घनेन हन्मि वृश्चिकम् अहिं दण्डेनागतम् ॥
16.15.m: Sapless here are the serpents, / those that are near and those that are far away; / with a club I strike the scorpion, / with a staff the approaching serpent.

16.15.s: aghāśvasyedaṃ bheṣajam ubhayoḥ svajasya ca | indro mahyam aghāyantam ahiṃ paidvo arundhayat ||
16.15.d: अघाश्वस्येदं भेषजम् उभयोः स्वजस्य च । इन्द्रो मह्यम् अघायन्तम् अहिं पैद्वो अरुन्धयत् ॥
16.15.m: This is Aghāśva's remedy / for both […]; / Indra obstructed for me / the malevolent serpent, [as did] the paidva-steed.

16.16.s: paidvasya manmahe vayaṃ sthirasya sthiradhāmnaḥ | ime paścāt pṛdākavaḥ pradīdhyata āsate ||
16.16.d: पैद्वस्य मन्महे वयं स्थिरस्य स्थिरधाम्नः । इमे पश्चात् पृदाकवः प्रदीध्यत आसते ॥
16.16.m: We contemplate the paidva-steed, / the firm, of firm abode; / these adders behind / sit brooding.

16.16.s: naṣṭāsavo naṣṭaviṣā hatā indreṇa vajriṇā | jaghānendro jaghnimā vayam ||
16.16.d: नष्टासवो नष्टविषा हता इन्द्रेण वज्रिणा । जघानेन्द्रो जघ्निमा वयम् ॥
16.16.m: Their breath lost, their poison lost, / slain by Indra with his thunderbolt; / Indra has slain them, we have slain them.

16.16.s: hatās tiraścirājayo nipiṣṭāsaḥ pṛdākavaḥ | darviṃ karikrataṃ śvitraṃ darbheṣv asitaṃ jahi ||
16.16.d: हतास् तिरश्चिराजयो निपिष्टासः पृदाकवः । दर्विं करिक्रतं श्वित्रं दर्भेष्व् असितं जहि ॥
16.16.m: Slain are the cross-striped [snakes], / crushed are the adders; / the hooded serpent, writhing, / kill among the darbha-grasses, the black one!

16.16.s: kairātikā kumārikā sakhā khanati bheṣajam | hiraṇyayībhir abhribhir girīṇām upa sānuṣu ||
16.16.d: कैरातिका कुमारिका सखा खनति भेषजम् । हिरण्ययीभिर् अभ्रिभिर् गिरीणाम् उप सानुषु ॥
16.16.m: A little Kirāta girl, / a friend, digs a remedy / with golden shovels / on the ridges of the mountains.

16.16.s: āyam agan yuvā bhiṣak pṛśnihāparājitaḥ | sa vai svajasya jambhana ubhayor vṛścikasya ca ||
16.16.d: आयम् अगन् युवा भिषक् पृश्निहापराजितः । स वै स्वजस्य जम्भन उभयोर् वृश्चिकस्य च ॥
16.16.m: Here has come the young physician, / the slayer of the dappled [serpent], unconquered; / he is indeed the crusher of the svaja-snake, / and of both, [the snake] and the scorpion.

16.16.s: indro me 'hīn ajambhayan mitraś ca varuṇaś ca | vātāparjanyobhā ||
16.16.d: इन्द्रो मे ऽहीन् अजम्भयन् मित्रश् च वरुणश् च । वातापर्जन्योभा ॥
16.16.m: Indra crushed the serpents for me, / and Mitra and Varuṇa, / and Vāta and Parjanya, both.

16.16.s: paidvo me 'hīn ajambhayat pṛdākūṃś ca pṛdākvaḥ | svajān tiraścirājīn kasarṇīlān daśonaśīn ||
16.16.d: पैद्वो मे ऽहीन् अजम्भयत् पृदाकूंश् च पृदाक्वः । स्वजान् तिरश्चिराजीन् कसर्णीलान् दशोनशीन् ॥
16.16.m: The paidva-steed crushed the serpents for me, / and the adders, male and female, / the svaja-snakes, the cross-striped ones, / the kasarṇīlas, the ten-biters.

16.16.s: indro jaghāna prathamo janitāram ahe tava | teṣāṃ vas tṛhyamāṇānāṃ kaḥ svit teṣām asad rasaḥ ||
16.16.d: इन्द्रो जघान प्रथमो जनितारम् अहे तव । तेषां वस् तृह्यमाणानां कः स्वित् तेषाम् असद् रसः ॥
16.16.m: Indra first slew / your progenitor, O serpent; / of those being crushed, / may their sap be gone!

16.16.s: saṃ hi śīrṣāṇy agrabhaṃ pauñjiṣṭa iva karvaram | sindhor madhyaṃ paretya vy anijam aher viṣam ||
16.16.d: सं हि शीर्षाण्य् अग्रभं पौञ्जिष्ट इव कर्वरम् । सिन्धोर् मध्यं परेत्य व्य् अनिजम् अहेर् विषम् ॥
16.16.m: For I have seized their heads, / like […] variegated; / having gone into the middle of the river, / I have washed off the serpent's poison.

16.16.s: ahīnāṃ sarveṣāṃ viṣaṃ parā vahantu sindhavaḥ | hatās tiraścirājayo nipiṣṭāsaḥ pṛdākavaḥ ||
16.16.d: अहीनां सर्वेषां विषं परा वहन्तु सिन्धवः । हतास् तिरश्चिराजयो निपिष्टासः पृदाकवः ॥
16.16.m: May the rivers wash away / the poison of all serpents; / slain are the cross-striped [snakes], / crushed are the adders.

16.17.s: oṣadhīnām ahaṃ vṛṇa urvarīr iva sādhuyā | nayāmy arvatīr iva ahe nir aitu te viṣam ||
16.17.d: ओषधीनाम् अहं वृण उर्वरीर् इव साधुया । नयाम्य् अर्वतीर् इव अहे निर् ऐतु ते विषम् ॥
16.17.m: I choose among the herbs, / properly as if [fertile] fields; / I lead them like mares: / O serpent, let your poison go out!

16.17.s: yad agnau sūrye viṣaṃ pṛthivyām oṣadhīṣu yat | kāndāviṣaṃ kaniklakaṃ nir aitv aitu te vahiḥ ||
16.17.d: यद् अग्नौ सूर्ये विषं पृथिव्याम् ओषधीषु यत् । कान्दाविषं कनिक्लकं निर् ऐत्व् ऐतु ते वहिः ॥
16.17.m: The poison that is in Agni, in the sun, / that which is in the earth, in the herbs, / the bulb-poison, the trembling poison— / let it go out, let it go out of you!

16.17.s: aṅgādaṅgāt pra cyāvaya hṛdayaṃ pari varjaya | adhā viṣasya yat tejo avācīnaṃ tad etu te ||
16.17.d: अङ्गादङ्गात् प्र च्यावय हृदयं परि वर्जय । अधा विषस्य यत् तेजो अवाचीनं तद् एतु ते ॥
16.17.m: Dislodge it from limb to limb; / spare the heart! / Now whatever force of the poison there is, / let that go downward from you.

16.17.s: agne trāyasva vimadaṃ nayemaṃ punar dhehi jīvase jātavedaḥ | mā te heḍāṃsi duritāva ganma māhir vadhīd viṣataḥ puruṣaṃ naḥ ||
16.17.d: अग्ने त्रायस्व विमदं नयेमं पुनर् धेहि जीवसे जातवेदः । मा ते हेडांसि दुरिताव गन्म माहिर् वधीद् विषतः पुरुषं नः ॥
16.17.m: O Agni, protect! Lead this man free from intoxication; / set him again to live, O Jātavedas! / May we not incur your angers and misfortunes; / may the serpent not slay our man with poison!

16.17.s: ye agnijā oṣadhijā ahīnāṃ ye abhrajā vidyuta ā babhūvuḥ | teṣāṃ jātāni bahudhā bahūni tebhyaḥ sarpebhyo namasā vidhema ||
16.17.d: ये अग्निजा ओषधिजा अहीनां ये अभ्रजा विद्युत आ बभूवुः । तेषां जातानि बहुधा बहूनि तेभ्यः सर्पेभ्यो नमसा विधेम ॥
16.17.m: Those serpents that are born of fire, born of plants, / that are born of the cloud, arisen from the lightning— / many and varied are their broods; / to those serpents let us do honor with homage!

16.17.s: taudī nāmāsi kanyā ghṛtācī nāma vā asi | adhaspadena te pador ā dade viṣadūṣaṇam ||
16.17.d: तौदी नामासि कन्या घृताची नाम वा असि । अधस्पदेन ते पदोर् आ ददे विषदूषणम् ॥
16.17.m: Taudī by name are you, a maiden, / or Ghṛtācī indeed by name are you. / Underneath the sole of your feet / I take the poison-spoiler.

16.17.s: āre abhūd viṣam araud viṣe viṣam aprāg api | agnir aher nir adhāg viṣaṃ somo nir aṇayīt | daṃṣṭāram anv agād viṣam ahir amṛta ||
16.17.d: आरे अभूद् विषम् अरौद् विषे विषम् अप्राग् अपि । अग्निर् अहेर् निर् अधाग् विषं सोमो निर् अणयीत् । दंष्टारम् अन्व् अगाद् विषम् अहिर् अमृत ॥
16.17.m: Far away has the poison gone; it has stopped; / the poison has dissolved into poison. / Agni has burnt out the serpent's poison, Soma has driven it away; / the poison has departed; the serpent has died.

16.18.s: kutas tau jātau katamaḥ so ardhaḥ kasmāl lokāt katarasyāḥ pṛthivyāḥ | vatsau virājaḥ salilād udaitāṃ tau tvā pṛcchāmi katareṇa dugdhā ||
16.18.d: कुतस् तौ जातौ कतमः सो अर्धः कस्माल् लोकात् कतरस्याः पृथिव्याः । वत्सौ विराजः सलिलाद् उदैतां तौ त्वा पृच्छामि कतरेण दुग्धा ॥
16.18.m: Whence were those two born? Which half was that? / From which world, from which of the two earths? / The two calves of Virāj arose from the watery flood: / I ask you, by which [of the two] was she milked?

16.18.s: yo 'krandayat salilaṃ mahitvā yoniṃ kṛtvā tribhujaṃ śayānam | vatsaḥ kāmadugho virājo guhā cakre tanvaḥ parācīḥ ||
16.18.d: यो ऽक्रन्दयत् सलिलं महित्वा योनिं कृत्वा त्रिभुजं शयानम् । वत्सः कामदुघो विराजो गुहा चक्रे तन्वः पराचीः ॥
16.18.m: He who made the watery flood roar through his greatness, / having made a three-angled womb lying [there]— / the calf, wish-milking, of Virāj, / concealed his bodies away.

16.18.s: yāni catvāri bṛhanti yeṣāṃ caturthaṃ viyunakti vācam | brahmainad vidyāt tapasā vipaścid yasminn ekaṃ yujyate yasminn ekam ||
16.18.d: यानि चत्वारि बृहन्ति येषां चतुर्थं वियुनक्ति वाचम् । ब्रह्मैनद् विद्यात् तपसा विपश्चिद् यस्मिन्न् एकं युज्यते यस्मिन्न् एकम् ॥
16.18.m: The four great [realms] / of which the fourth divides speech— / let the wise priest know this by fervor: / in which the one is joined, in which the one [is set].

16.18.s: bṛhataḥ pari sāmāni ṣaṣṭhāt pañcādhi nirmitā | bṛhad bṛhatyā nirmitaṃ kuto 'dhi bṛhatī mitā ||
16.18.d: बृहतः परि सामानि षष्ठात् पञ्चाधि निर्मिता । बृहद् बृहत्या निर्मितं कुतो ऽधि बृहती मिता ॥
16.18.m: The sāmans are fashioned out of the Bṛhat, / from the sixth over the fifth. / The Bṛhat is fashioned from the Bṛhatī: / from what was the Bṛhatī measured?

16.18.s: bṛhatī pari mātrāyā mātur mātrādhi nirmitā | māyā hi jajñe māyāyā māyāyā mātalī pari ||
16.18.d: बृहती परि मात्राया मातुर् मात्राधि निर्मिता । माया हि जज्ञे मायाया मायाया मातली परि ॥
16.18.m: The Bṛhatī was fashioned out of measure, / out of the mother's measure. / For magic was born of magic, / from magic [came] Mātali.

16.18.s: vaiśvānarasya pratimopari dyaur yāvad rodasī vibabādhe agniḥ | tataḥ ṣaṣṭhād āmuto yanti stomā ud ito yanty abhi ṣaṣṭham ahnaḥ ||
16.18.d: वैश्वानरस्य प्रतिमोपरि द्यौर् यावद् रोदसी विबबाधे अग्निः । ततः षष्ठाद् आमुतो यन्ति स्तोमा उद् इतो यन्त्य् अभि षष्ठम् अह्नः ॥
16.18.m: The sky above is the counterpart of Vaiśvānara, / as far as Agni forced the two world-halves apart. / From there, from that [world], the stomata go from the sixth; / from here they go upward toward the sixth [day] of the day.

16.18.s: ṣaṭ ṭvā pṛcchāma ṛṣayaḥ kaśyapedaṃ tvaṃ hi yuktaṃ yuyukṣe yogyaṃ ca | virājam āhur brahmaṇaḥ pitaraṃ tāṃ no vi dhehy ṛtuthā sakhibhyaḥ ||
16.18.d: षट् ट्वा पृच्छाम ऋषयः कश्यपेदं त्वं हि युक्तं युयुक्षे योग्यं च । विराजम् आहुर् ब्रह्मणः पितरं तां नो वि धेह्य् ऋतुथा सखिभ्यः ॥
16.18.m: We six ṛṣis ask you this, O Kaśyapa, / for you wish to yoke what is yoked and what is fit to be yoked: / they call Virāj the father of sacred knowledge; / distribute her to us, your comrades, in due season!

16.18.s: yāṃ pracyutām anu yajñāḥ pracyuvanta upatiṣṭhanta upatiṣṭhamānām | tasyā vraje prasave yakṣam ejati sā virāḍ ṛṣayaḥ parame vyoman ||
16.18.d: यां प्रच्युताम् अनु यज्ञाः प्रच्युवन्त उपतिष्ठन्त उपतिष्ठमानाम् । तस्या व्रजे प्रसवे यक्षम् एजति सा विराड् ऋषयः परमे व्योमन् ॥
16.18.m: After whom when she moved forth the sacrifices moved forth, / whom they attended as she stood— / in her pen, in her bringing-forth, an apparition stirs: / she is Virāj, O ṛṣis, in the highest firmament.

16.18.s: aprāṇaiti prāṇena prāṇatīnāṃ virāṭ svarājam abhy eti paścāt | viśvaṃ mṛśantīm abhirūpāṃ virājaṃ paśyanti tve na tve paśyanty enām ||
16.18.d: अप्राणैति प्राणेन प्राणतीनां विराट् स्वराजम् अभ्य् एति पश्चात् । विश्वं मृशन्तीम् अभिरूपां विराजं पश्यन्ति त्वे न त्वे पश्यन्त्य् एनाम् ॥
16.18.m: Breathless she goes by the breath of breathing things; / Virāj approaches Svarāj from behind. / Virāj, touching the all, perfectly formed— / some see her, some do not see her.

16.18.s: ko virājo mithunatvaṃ pra veda ka ṛtūn ka u kalpam asyāḥ | kramān ko asyā bahudhā vidugdhān ko asyā dhāma katidhā vyuṣṭīḥ ||
16.18.d: को विराजो मिथुनत्वं प्र वेद क ऋतून् क उ कल्पम् अस्याः । क्रमान् को अस्या बहुधा विदुग्धान् को अस्या धाम कतिधा व्युष्टीः ॥
16.18.m: Who knows the pair-nature of Virāj? / Who her seasons, who her rite? / Who knows her steps milked out in many ways? / Who her station, how many her dawnings?

16.19.s: iyam eva sā yā prathamā vyaucchat sāpsv antaś carati praviṣṭā | vadhūr jigāya navagaj janitrī mahānto asyāṃ mahimāno antaḥ ||
16.19.d: इयम् एव सा या प्रथमा व्यौच्छत् साप्स्व् अन्तश् चरति प्रविष्टा । वधूर् जिगाय नवगज् जनित्री महान्तो अस्यां महिमानो अन्तः ॥
16.19.m: This indeed is she who first shone forth; / she moves having entered into the waters. / The bride, the mother of nine, has conquered; / great are the greatnesses within her.

16.19.s: chandaḥpakṣe uṣasā pepiśāne samānīṃ yonim anu saṃ carete | sūryapatnī saṃ carataḥ prajānatī ketumatī ajare bhūriretasā ||
16.19.d: छन्दःपक्षे उषसा पेपिशाने समानीं योनिम् अनु सं चरेते । सूर्यपत्नी सं चरतः प्रजानती केतुमती अजरे भूरिरेतसा ॥
16.19.m: The two Dawns, meter-winged, richly adorned, / move together along a common womb. / The two wives of the sun move together, knowing, / possessors of banners, unaging, rich in seed.

16.19.s: ṛtasya panthām anu tisra āgus trayo gharmā anu reta āguḥ | prajām ekā jinvaty ūrjam ekā rāṣṭram ekā rakṣati devayūnām ||
16.19.d: ऋतस्य पन्थाम् अनु तिस्र आगुस् त्रयो घर्मा अनु रेत आगुः । प्रजाम् एका जिन्वत्य् ऊर्जम् एका राष्ट्रम् एका रक्षति देवयूनाम् ॥
16.19.m: Along the path of truth three have come; / three heats have come following the seed. / One quickens the offspring, one nourishment, / one protects the kingdom of the god-seeking.

16.19.s: agnīṣṭomam adadhur yā turīyāsīd yajñasya pakṣām ṛṣayaḥ kalpayantaḥ | gāyatrīṃ triṣṭubhaṃ jagatīm anuṣṭubhaṃ bṛhadarkīṃ yajamānāya svar ābharantaḥ ||
16.19.d: अग्नीष्टोमम् अदधुर् या तुरीयासीद् यज्ञस्य पक्षाम् ऋषयः कल्पयन्तः । गायत्रीं त्रिष्टुभं जगतीम् अनुष्टुभं बृहदर्कीं यजमानाय स्वर् आभरन्तः ॥
16.19.m: They established the Agniṣṭoma, who was the fourth, / the ṛṣis fashioning the wings of the sacrifice, / bringing the Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh, Jagatī, Anuṣṭubh, / [and] the Bṛhadarka, heaven for the sacrificer.

16.19.s: pañca vyuṣṭīr anu pañca dohā gāṃ pañcanāmnīm ṛtavo 'nu pañca | pañca diśaḥ pañcadaśena kḷptās tā ekamūrdhnīr abhi lokam ekam ||
16.19.d: पञ्च व्युष्टीर् अनु पञ्च दोहा गां पञ्चनाम्नीम् ऋतवो ऽनु पञ्च । पञ्च दिशः पञ्चदशेन कॢप्तास् ता एकमूर्ध्नीर् अभि लोकम् एकम् ॥
16.19.m: Following the five dawnings are five milkings; / the seasons follow the cow of five names; / the five directions are arranged by the fifteen-fold: / they, single-headed, [turn] toward a single world.

16.19.s: ṣaḍ jātā bhūtā prathamaja rtasya ṣaḍ u sāmāni ṣaḍahaṃ vahanti | ṣaḍyogaṃ sīram anu sāmasāma ṣaḍ āhur dyāvāpṛthivī ṣaḍ urvīḥ ||
16.19.d: षड् जाता भूता प्रथमज र्तस्य षड् उ सामानि षडहं वहन्ति । षड्योगं सीरम् अनु सामसाम षड् आहुर् द्यावापृथिवी षड् उर्वीः ॥
16.19.m: Six are born, beings, firstborn of truth; / and six sāmans bear the six-day rite. / A six-yoked plow follows chant upon chant; / they say there are six heaven-and-earths, six.

16.19.s: ṣaḍ āhuḥ śītān ṣaḍ u māsa uṣṇān ṛtūn no brūta yatamo 'tiriktaḥ | sapta suparṇāḥ kavayo ni ṣeduḥ sapta chandāṃsy anu sapta dīkṣāḥ ||
16.19.d: षड् आहुः शीतान् षड् उ मास उष्णान् ऋतून् नो ब्रूत यतमो ऽतिरिक्तः । सप्त सुपर्णाः कवयो नि षेदुः सप्त छन्दांस्य् अनु सप्त दीक्षाः ॥
16.19.m: They say six are cold and six months are hot: / tell us the seasons, which one is left over? / Seven well-winged poets have sat down; / following seven meters are seven consecrations.

16.19.s: sapta homāḥ samidho ha sapta madhūni saptartavo nu sapta | saptājyāni pari bhūtam āyan sapta hotāra ṛtuthā yajanti tāḥ saptagṛdhrā iti śuśravāham ||
16.19.d: सप्त होमाः समिधो ह सप्त मधूनि सप्तर्तवो नु सप्त । सप्ताज्यानि परि भूतम् आयन् सप्त होतार ऋतुथा यजन्ति ताः सप्तगृध्रा इति शुश्रवाहम् ॥
16.19.m: Seven are the oblations, seven indeed the kindling sticks, / seven the sweets, seven indeed the seasons. / Seven melted butters went around being; / seven Hotṛs sacrifice in due season: / these are the ‘seven vultures’.

16.19.s: aṣṭau dhāmāni prathamaja rtasya aṣṭendrartvijo daivyā ye | aṣṭayonir aditir aṣṭaputrā aṣṭamīṃ rātrim abhi havyam eti ||
16.19.d: अष्टौ धामानि प्रथमज र्तस्य अष्टेन्द्रर्त्विजो दैव्या ये । अष्टयोनिर् अदितिर् अष्टपुत्रा अष्टमीं रात्रिम् अभि हव्यम् एति ॥
16.19.m: Eight are the stations, O firstborn of truth, / eight are the divine priests of Indra. / Aditi has eight wombs, eight sons; / toward the eighth night the oblation goes.

16.19.s: itthaṃ śreyo manyamānedam āgāṃ yuṣmākaṃ sakhye aham asmi śevā | samānajanmā kratur astu vaḥ śivaḥ sa naḥ sarvāḥ saṃ carati prajānan ||
16.19.d: इत्थं श्रेयो मन्यमानेदम् आगां युष्माकं सख्ये अहम् अस्मि शेवा । समानजन्मा क्रतुर् अस्तु वः शिवः स नः सर्वाः सं चरति प्रजानन् ॥
16.19.m: Thinking thus the better, I have come here; / in your friendship I am gracious. / May your will of common birth be auspicious; / knowing, he moves through all of us.

16.20.s: kevalīndrāya duduhe hi gṛṣṭir vaśaṃ pīyūṣaṃ prathamaṃ duhānā | athātarpayac caturaś caturdhā devān manuṣyām̐ asurān utarṣīn ||
16.20.d: केवलीन्द्राय दुदुहे हि गृष्टिर् वशं पीयूषं प्रथमं दुहाना । अथातर्पयच् चतुरश् चतुर्धा देवान् मनुष्याँ असुरान् उतर्षीन् ॥
16.20.m: For the heifer was milked for Indra alone, / milking out at first her will, the colostrum. / Then she satisfied fourfold the four: / the gods, men, Asuras, and ṛṣis.

16.20.s: aṣṭendrasya ṣaḍ yamasya ṛṣīṇāṃ sapta saptadhā | apo manuṣyān oṣadhīs tān u pañcānu secire ||
16.20.d: अष्टेन्द्रस्य षड् यमस्य ऋषीणां सप्त सप्तधा । अपो मनुष्यान् ओषधीस् तान् उ पञ्चानु सेचिरे ॥
16.20.m: Eight of Indra, six of Yama, / seven of the ṛṣis, sevenfold: / waters, men, plants— / those five poured out after them.

16.20.s: ko nu gauḥ ka ekarṣiḥ kim u sāma kā āśiṣaḥ | yakṣmaṃ pṛthivyām ekavṛd ekartuḥ katamo nu saḥ ||
16.20.d: को नु गौः क एकर्षिः किम् उ साम का आशिषः । यक्ष्मं पृथिव्याम् एकवृद् एकर्तुः कतमो नु सः ॥
16.20.m: Who then is the cow? Who is the single ṛṣi? / What is the sāman? What are the blessings? / The single fold, the pulmonary disease on earth— / which one then is the single season?

16.20.s: eko gaur eka ekarṣir ekaṃ sāmaikadhāśiṣaḥ | yakṣmaṃ pṛthivyām ekavṛd ekartur nāti ricyate ||
16.20.d: एको गौर् एक एकर्षिर् एकं सामैकधाशिषः । यक्ष्मं पृथिव्याम् एकवृद् एकर्तुर् नाति रिच्यते ॥
16.20.m: One is the cow, one the single ṛṣi; / one is the sāman, singly are the blessings. / The single fold, the pulmonary disease on earth— / the single season does not exceed.

16.21.s: prāṇāya namo yasya sarvam idaṃ vaśe | yo bhūtaḥ sarvasyeśvaro yasmin sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam ||
16.21.d: प्राणाय नमो यस्य सर्वम् इदं वशे । यो भूतः सर्वस्येश्वरो यस्मिन् सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
16.21.m: Homage to Breath, / in whose power is all this, / who has become the lord of all, / in whom all is established!

16.21.s: namas te prāṇa krandāya namas te stanayitnave | namas te astu vidyute namas te prāṇa varṣate ||
16.21.d: नमस् ते प्राण क्रन्दाय नमस् ते स्तनयित्नवे । नमस् ते अस्तु विद्युते नमस् ते प्राण वर्षते ॥
16.21.m: Homage to you, O Breath, when roaring; / homage to you when thundering; / homage be to your lightning; / homage to you, O Breath, when raining!

16.21.s: yat prāṇa ṛtāv āgate abhikrandaty oṣadhīḥ | pra vīyante garbhaṃ dadhate atho bahvīr vi jāyante ||
16.21.d: यत् प्राण ऋताव् आगते अभिक्रन्दत्य् ओषधीः । प्र वीयन्ते गर्भं दधते अथो बह्वीर् वि जायन्ते ॥
16.21.m: When Breath, the season having arrived, / roars upon the plants, / they are impregnated, they receive the embryo, / and then in abundance they are born.

16.21.s: yat prāṇa stanayitnunā abhikrandaty oṣadhīḥ | sarvaṃ tadā pra modate yad u kiṃ ca bhūmyām adhi ||
16.21.d: यत् प्राण स्तनयित्नुना अभिक्रन्दत्य् ओषधीः । सर्वं तदा प्र मोदते यद् उ किं च भूम्याम् अधि ॥
16.21.m: When Breath with thunder / roars upon the plants, / then everything rejoices, / whatever is upon the earth.

16.21.s: yadā prāṇo abhyakrandīd varṣeṇa stanayitnunā | paśavas tat pra modante maho vai no bhaviṣyati ||
16.21.d: यदा प्राणो अभ्यक्रन्दीद् वर्षेण स्तनयित्नुना । पशवस् तत् प्र मोदन्ते महो वै नो भविष्यति ॥
16.21.m: When Breath has roared / with rain [and] with thunder, / the cattle then rejoice: / ‘Great indeed will be our [fortune]!’

16.21.s: abhivṛṣṭā oṣadhayaḥ prāṇena sam avādiran | āyur vai naḥ prātītarat sarvā naḥ surabhīr akaḥ ||
16.21.d: अभिवृष्टा ओषधयः प्राणेन सम् अवादिरन् । आयुर् वै नः प्रातीतरत् सर्वा नः सुरभीर् अकः ॥
16.21.m: Rained upon, the plants / conversed together with Breath: / ‘You have prolonged our life indeed; / you have made us all fragrant.’

16.21.s: namas te prāṇa prāṇate namo astv apānate | pratīcīnāya te namaḥ parācīnāya te namaḥ sarvasmai ta idaṃ namaḥ ||
16.21.d: नमस् ते प्राण प्राणते नमो अस्त्व् अपानते । प्रतीचीनाय ते नमः पराचीनाय ते नमः सर्वस्मै त इदं नमः ॥
16.21.m: Homage to you, O Breath, when breathing in; / homage be [to you] when breathing out! / Homage to you facing toward; / homage to you facing away; / to all of you be this homage!

16.21.s: namas te astv āyate namo astu parāyate | namas te prāṇa tiṣṭhata āsīnāyota te namaḥ ||
16.21.d: नमस् ते अस्त्व् आयते नमो अस्तु परायते । नमस् ते प्राण तिष्ठत आसीनायोत ते नमः ॥
16.21.m: Homage be to you coming; / homage be [to you] departing! / Homage to you, O Breath, standing, / and homage to you seated!

16.21.s: yā te prāṇa priyā tanū yā vā te prāṇa preyasī | atho yad bheṣajaṃ tava tasya no dhehi jīvase ||
16.21.d: या ते प्राण प्रिया तनू या वा ते प्राण प्रेयसी । अथो यद् भेषजं तव तस्य नो धेहि जीवसे ॥
16.21.m: That body of yours, O Breath, which is dear, / or that which is dearer, O Breath, / and whatever remedy of yours [there is]— / bestow of that on us for living!

16.21.s: prāṇaḥ prajā anu vaste pitā putram iva priyam | prāṇo ha sarvasyeśvaro yac ca prāṇati yac ca na ||
16.21.d: प्राणः प्रजा अनु वस्ते पिता पुत्रम् इव प्रियम् । प्राणो ह सर्वस्येश्वरो यच् च प्राणति यच् च न ॥
16.21.m: Breath [attends] upon the creatures / as a father upon his dear son. / Breath is indeed the lord of all, / both of what breathes and what does not.

16.22.s: prāṇo mṛtyuḥ prāṇo amṛtaṃ prāṇaṃ devā upāsate | prāṇo ha satyavādinam uttame loka ā dadhat ||
16.22.d: प्राणो मृत्युः प्राणो अमृतं प्राणं देवा उपासते । प्राणो ह सत्यवादिनम् उत्तमे लोक आ दधत् ॥
16.22.m: Breath is death, Breath is immortality; / the gods worship Breath. / Breath indeed establishes the speaker of truth / in the highest world.

16.22.s: prāṇo virāṭ prāṇo deṣṭrī prāṇaṃ sarvā upāsate | prāṇo 'gniś candramāḥ sūryaḥ prāṇam āhuḥ prajāpatim ||
16.22.d: प्राणो विराट् प्राणो देष्ट्री प्राणं सर्वा उपासते । प्राणो ऽग्निश् चन्द्रमाः सूर्यः प्राणम् आहुः प्रजापतिम् ॥
16.22.m: Breath is Virāj, Breath is the director; / all [creatures] worship Breath. / Breath is Agni, the Moon, the Sun; / they call Breath Prajāpati.

16.22.s: prāṇāpānau vrīhayavāv anaḍvān prāṇa ucyate | yave ha prāṇa āhito apāno vrīhir ucyate ||
16.22.d: प्राणापानौ व्रीहयवाव् अनड्वान् प्राण उच्यते । यवे ह प्राण आहितो अपानो व्रीहिर् उच्यते ॥
16.22.m: Inhaling and exhaling are rice and barley; / Breath is called the draft-ox. / In barley indeed is breath deposited; / downward-breath is called rice.

16.22.s: apānati prāṇati puruṣo garbhe antaḥ | yadā tvaṃ prāṇa jinvasy atha sa jāyate tvat ||
16.22.d: अपानति प्राणति पुरुषो गर्भे अन्तः । यदा त्वं प्राण जिन्वस्य् अथ स जायते त्वत् ॥
16.22.m: [A person] exhales [and] inhales, / a person inside the womb. / When you, O Breath, quicken [him], / then he is born from you.

16.22.s: prāṇam āhur mātariśvānaṃ vāto ha prāṇa ucyate | prāṇe ha bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ ca prāṇe sarvaṃ samāhitam ||
16.22.d: प्राणम् आहुर् मातरिश्वानं वातो ह प्राण उच्यते । प्राणे ह भूतं भव्यं च प्राणे सर्वं समाहितम् ॥
16.22.m: They call Breath Mātariśvan; / wind indeed is called Breath. / In Breath indeed is the past and the future; / in Breath is everything established.

16.22.s: ātharvaṇīr āṅgirasīr daivīr manuṣyajāś ca yāḥ | sarvāḥ pra modanta oṣadhīr yadā tvaṃ prāṇa jinvasi ||
16.22.d: आथर्वणीर् आङ्गिरसीर् दैवीर् मनुष्यजाश् च याः । सर्वाः प्र मोदन्त ओषधीर् यदा त्वं प्राण जिन्वसि ॥
16.22.m: Those [plants] of Atharvan, of Aṅgiras, / those of the gods, and those born of men— / all of them rejoice / when you, O Breath, quicken [them].

16.22.s: yadā prāṇo abhyavarṣīd varṣeṇa pṛthivīṃ mahīm | oṣadhayaḥ pra modante atho yāḥ kāś ca vīrudhaḥ ||
16.22.d: यदा प्राणो अभ्यवर्षीद् वर्षेण पृथिवीं महीम् । ओषधयः प्र मोदन्ते अथो याः काश् च वीरुधः ॥
16.22.m: When Breath rains down / with rain upon the great earth, / the herbs rejoice, / and whatever plants [there are].

16.22.s: yas te prāṇedaṃ veda yasmiṃś cāsi pratiṣṭhitaḥ | sarve asmai baliṃ harān amuṣmiṃl loka uttame ||
16.22.d: यस् ते प्राणेदं वेद यस्मिंश् चासि प्रतिष्ठितः । सर्वे अस्मै बलिं हरान् अमुष्मिंल् लोक उत्तमे ॥
16.22.m: Whoever knows this of you, O Breath, / and on what you are supported— / to him all shall bring tribute / in yonder highest world.

16.22.s: yathā prāṇa balihṛtas tubhyaṃ sarvāḥ prajā imāḥ | evā tasmai baliṃ harān yas tvā śuśrāva śuśruvuḥ ||
16.22.d: यथा प्राण बलिहृतस् तुभ्यं सर्वाः प्रजा इमाः । एवा तस्मै बलिं हरान् यस् त्वा शुश्राव शुश्रुवुः ॥
16.22.m: Just as all these creatures, O Breath, / are bringers of tribute to you, / even so let them bring tribute to him / who has heard you, [and] who have heard [you].

16.22.s: antargarbhaś carati devatāsv ābhūto bhūtaḥ sa u jāyate punaḥ | sa bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhuvanaṃ bhaviṣyat pitā putraṃ pra viveśā śacībhiḥ ||
16.22.d: अन्तर्गर्भश् चरति देवतास्व् आभूतो भूतः स उ जायते पुनः । स भूतं भव्यं भुवनं भविष्यत् पिता पुत्रं प्र विवेशा शचीभिः ॥
16.22.m: Moving as an inner embryo among the deities, / become manifest, having become, he is born again. / He [as] the past, the future, the world, [and] what is to be, / [as] a father has entered his son through [his] powers.

16.23.s: ekaṃ padaṃ not khidati salilād dhaṃsa utpatan | yad aṅga sa tam utkhiden naivādya na śvo na rātrī nāhaḥ syān na prajñāyaiti kiṃ cana ||
16.23.d: एकं पदं नोत् खिदति सलिलाद् धंस उत्पतन् । यद् अङ्ग स तम् उत्खिदेन् नैवाद्य न श्वो न रात्री नाहः स्यान् न प्रज्ञायैति किं चन ॥
16.23.m: He does not draw out one foot / when rising from the water, the wild goose. / For if indeed he were to draw it out, / neither / neither night nor day would exist, / nor would anything at all be discerned.

16.23.s: aṣṭācakraṃ vartata ekanemi sahasrākṣaraṃ pra puro ni paścāt | ardhenedaṃ pari babhūva viśvaṃ yad asyārdhaṃ katamaḥ sa ketuḥ ||
16.23.d: अष्टाचक्रं वर्तत एकनेमि सहस्राक्षरं प्र पुरो नि पश्चात् । अर्धेनेदं परि बभूव विश्वं यद् अस्यार्धं कतमः स केतुः ॥
16.23.m: Eight-wheeled it rolls, with a single felly, / thousand-syllabled, forward in front, down behind. / With one half it has encompassed this universe; / what its [other] half is—which banner is that?

16.23.s: yo asya viśvajanmana īśe sarvasya ceṣṭataḥ | anyeṣu kṣipradhanvane tasmai prāṇa namo 'stu te ||
16.23.d: यो अस्य विश्वजन्मन ईशे सर्वस्य चेष्टतः । अन्येषु क्षिप्रधन्वने तस्मै प्राण नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
16.23.m: He who rules over this all-engendering, / moving whole— / [who is] swift-bowed among others: / to that one, O Breath, homage be to you!

16.23.s: yo asya sarvajanmana īśe viśvasya ceṣṭataḥ | atandro brahmaṇā dhīraḥ prāṇo mām abhi rakṣatu ||
16.23.d: यो अस्य सर्वजन्मन ईशे विश्वस्य चेष्टतः । अतन्द्रो ब्रह्मणा धीरः प्राणो माम् अभि रक्षतु ॥
16.23.m: He who rules over this all-engendering, / moving universe— / untiring, wise through sacred lore, / may Breath protect me all around!

16.23.s: ūrdhvaḥ supteṣu jāgāra nanu tīryaṅ ni padyate | na suptam asya supteṣv anu śuśrāva kaś cana ||
16.23.d: ऊर्ध्वः सुप्तेषु जागार ननु तीर्यङ् नि पद्यते । न सुप्तम् अस्य सुप्तेष्व् अनु शुश्राव कश् चन ॥
16.23.m: Upright he wakes among those who sleep; / surely he does not fall prostrate. / No one has heard of his sleeping / among those who sleep.

16.23.s: prāṇa mā mat paryāvṛto na mad anyo bhaviṣyasi | apāṃ garbham iva jīvase prāṇa badhnāmi tvā mayi ||
16.23.d: प्राण मा मत् पर्यावृतो न मद् अन्यो भविष्यसि । अपां गर्भम् इव जीवसे प्राण बध्नामि त्वा मयि ॥
16.23.m: O Breath, do not turn away; / you shall not be another. / Like the embryo of the waters, for living, / O Breath, I bind you in myself.

16.24.s: sāhasras tveṣa ṛṣabhaḥ payasvān viśvā rūpāṇi vakṣaṇāsu bibhrat | bhadraṃ dātre yajamānāya śikṣan bārhaspatya usriyas tantum ātān ||
16.24.d: साहस्रस् त्वेष ऋषभः पयस्वान् विश्वा रूपाणि वक्षणासु बिभ्रत् । भद्रं दात्रे यजमानाय शिक्षन् बार्हस्पत्य उस्रियस् तन्तुम् आतान् ॥
16.24.m: Belonging to a thousand, vehement, the bull full of milk, / bearing all forms in his belly, / bestowing good on the giver, on the sacrificer, / the bull belonging to Bṛhaspati [extends] the thread […].

16.24.s: apāṃ yo agre pratimā babhūva prabhūḥ sarvasmai pṛthivīva devī | pitā vatsānāṃ patir aghnyānāṃ sāhasre poṣe api naḥ kṛṇotu ||
16.24.d: अपां यो अग्रे प्रतिमा बभूव प्रभूः सर्वस्मै पृथिवीव देवी । पिता वत्सानां पतिर् अघ्न्यानां साहस्रे पोषे अपि नः कृणोतु ॥
16.24.m: He who in the beginning became the counterpart of the waters, / prevailing for everything like the divine earth, / father of calves, lord of cows not to be slain, / let him place us in thousandfold thriving!

16.24.s: pumān antarvān sthaviraḥ payasvān vasoḥ kabandham ṛṣabho bibharti | tam indrāya pathibhir devayānair hutam agnir vahatu jātavedāḥ ||
16.24.d: पुमान् अन्तर्वान् स्थविरः पयस्वान् वसोः कबन्धम् ऋषभो बिभर्ति । तम् इन्द्राय पथिभिर् देवयानैर् हुतम् अग्निर् वहतु जातवेदाः ॥
16.24.m: A male pregnant, stout, rich in milk, / the bull carries the barrel of the good [fluid]. / Offered to Indra by the paths traveled by gods, / let Agni Jātavedas convey him!

16.24.s: devānāṃ bhāga upanāha eṣo apāṃ rasa oṣadhīnāṃ ghṛtasya | somasya drapsam avṛṇīta śakro bṛhann adrir abhavad yac charīram ||
16.24.d: देवानां भाग उपनाह एषो अपां रस ओषधीनां घृतस्य । सोमस्य द्रप्सम् अवृणीत शक्रो बृहन्न् अद्रिर् अभवद् यच् छरीरम् ॥
16.24.m: This is the share, the wrapper of the gods, / the sap of the waters, of the plants, of ghee. / Śakra chose the drop of Soma; / the great rock became [his] body.

16.24.s: pitā vatsānāṃ patir aghnyānām atho pitā mahatāṃ gargarāṇām | vatso jarāyuḥ pratidhuk pīyūṣa āmikṣā ghṛtaṃ tad v asya retaḥ ||
16.24.d: पिता वत्सानां पतिर् अघ्न्यानाम् अथो पिता महतां गर्गराणाम् । वत्सो जरायुः प्रतिधुक् पीयूष आमिक्षा घृतं तद् व् अस्य रेतः ॥
16.24.m: Father of calves, lord of cows not to be slain, / and father of great churning-pots; / calf, afterbirth, fresh milk, biestings, / clotted curds, ghee—that indeed is his seed.

16.24.s: somasya pūrṇaṃ kalaśaṃ bibharṣi tvaṣṭā rūpāṇāṃ janitā paśūnām | śivās te santu prajanva imā ny asmabhyaṃ svadhite yaccha yā amūḥ ||
16.24.d: सोमस्य पूर्णं कलशं बिभर्षि त्वष्टा रूपाणां जनिता पशूनाम् । शिवास् ते सन्तु प्रजन्व इमा न्य् अस्मभ्यं स्वधिते यच्छ या अमूः ॥
16.24.m: You carry the full vessel of Soma, / Tvaṣṭṛ, the begetter of forms [and] cattle. / May these mothers be kindly to you; / bestow those on us, O axe!

16.24.s: indrasyaujo varuṇasya bāhū aśvinor aṃsau marutām iyaṃ kakut | bṛhaspatisaṃbhṛtam etam āhur ye dhīrāsaḥ kavayo ye manīṣiṇaḥ ||
16.24.d: इन्द्रस्यौजो वरुणस्य बाहू अश्विनोर् अंसौ मरुताम् इयं ककुत् । बृहस्पतिसंभृतम् एतम् आहुर् ये धीरासः कवयो ये मनीषिणः ॥
16.24.m: Indra's vigor, Varuṇa's two arms, / the Aśvins' two shoulders, this hump of the Maruts: / they call him brought together by Bṛhaspati, / those who are wise, the poets, the thinkers.

16.24.s: ājyaṃ bibharti ghṛtam asya retaḥ sāhasraḥ poṣas tam u yajñam āhuḥ | indrasya rūpam ṛṣabho vasānaḥ so asmāṃ devāḥ śiva aitu dattaḥ ||
16.24.d: आज्यं बिभर्ति घृतम् अस्य रेतः साहस्रः पोषस् तम् उ यज्ञम् आहुः । इन्द्रस्य रूपम् ऋषभो वसानः सो अस्मां देवाः शिव ऐतु दत्तः ॥
16.24.m: He bears melted butter; ghee is his seed; / thousandfold thriving—that indeed they call the sacrifice. / The bull, clothing himself in the form of Indra— / let him, given, come to us auspiciously, O gods!

16.24.s: daivīr viśaḥ payasvān ā tanoṣi tvām indraṃ tvāṃ sarasvantam āhuḥ | sahasraṃ sa ekamukhā dadāti yo brāhmaṇa ṛṣabham ā juhoti ||
16.24.d: दैवीर् विशः पयस्वान् आ तनोषि त्वाम् इन्द्रं त्वां सरस्वन्तम् आहुः । सहस्रं स एकमुखा ददाति यो ब्राह्मण ऋषभम् आ जुहोति ॥
16.24.m: Rich in milk, you extend the divine clans; / they call you Indra, they call you Sarasvant. / A thousand of one facing he gives, / who offers up the bull to a Brahmin.

16.24.s: bṛhaspatiḥ savitā te mano dadhau tvaṣṭur vāyoḥ pary ātmā ta ābhṛtaḥ | antarikṣe manasā tvā juhomi barhiṣ ṭe dyāvāpṛthivī abhūtām ||
16.24.d: बृहस्पतिः सविता ते मनो दधौ त्वष्टुर् वायोः पर्य् आत्मा त आभृतः । अन्तरिक्षे मनसा त्वा जुहोमि बर्हिष् टे द्यावापृथिवी अभूताम् ॥
16.24.m: Bṛhaspati [and] Savitṛ established your mind; / your self was brought from Tvaṣṭṛ [and] Vāyu. / In the intermediate space I offer you with my mind; / let Heaven and Earth be your sacrificial grass!

16.25.s: ya indra iva deveṣv eti goṣu vivāvadat | tasya ṛṣabhasyāṅgāni brahmā saṃ stautu bhadrayā ||
16.25.d: य इन्द्र इव देवेष्व् एति गोषु विवावदत् । तस्य ऋषभस्याङ्गानि ब्रह्मा सं स्तौतु भद्रया ॥
16.25.m: He who, like Indra among the gods, / goes lowing loudly among the cows— / of that bull, let the hotṛ priest / praise the limbs with auspicious [speech]!

16.25.s: pārśve āstām anumatyā bhagasyāstām anūvṛjau | aṣṭhīvantāv abravīn mitro mamaitau kevalāv iti ||
16.25.d: पार्श्वे आस्ताम् अनुमत्या भगस्यास्ताम् अनूवृजौ । अष्ठीवन्ताव् अब्रवीन् मित्रो ममैतौ केवलाव् इति ॥
16.25.m: The two flanks belonged to Anumati; / the two flanks belonged to Bhaga. / Mitra said of the two knees: / 'These two are solely mine.'

16.25.s: bhasad āsīd ādityānāṃ śroṇī āstāṃ bṛhaspateḥ | pucchaṃ vātasya devasya tena dhūnoty oṣadhīḥ ||
16.25.d: भसद् आसीद् आदित्यानां श्रोणी आस्तां बृहस्पतेः । पुच्छं वातस्य देवस्य तेन धूनोत्य् ओषधीः ॥
16.25.m: The rump belonged to the Ādityas; / the two hips belonged to Bṛhaspati. / The tail belongs to the god Vāta; / with it he shakes the herbs.

16.25.s: kroḍa āsīj jāmiśaṃsasya somasya kalaśo dhṛtaḥ | utthātur abruvan pado yad ṛṣabhaṃ vyakalpayan ||
16.25.d: क्रोड आसीज् जामिशंसस्य सोमस्य कलशो धृतः । उत्थातुर् अब्रुवन् पदो यद् ऋषभं व्यकल्पयन् ॥
16.25.m: The chest [belonged] to Jāmiśaṃsa; / the vessel of Soma was held [fast]. / They said the legs belonged to the one who rises up, / when they partitioned the bull.

16.25.s: gudā āsan sinīvālyāḥ sūryāyās tvacam abruvan | devāḥ saṃgatya yat sarva ṛṣabhaṃ vyakalpayan ||
16.25.d: गुदा आसन् सिनीवाल्याः सूर्यायास् त्वचम् अब्रुवन् । देवाः संगत्य यत् सर्व ऋषभं व्यकल्पयन् ॥
16.25.m: The intestines belonged to Sinīvālī; / they declared the skin to belong to Sūryā, / when all the gods, having assembled, / partitioned the bull.

16.25.s: te kuṣṭhikāḥ saramāyai kūrmebhyo adadhuḥ śaphān | ūbadhyam asya kīṭebhyaś śvavartebhyo adhārayan ||
16.25.d: ते कुष्ठिकाः सरमायै कूर्मेभ्यो अदधुः शफान् । ऊबध्यम् अस्य कीटेभ्यश् श्ववर्तेभ्यो अधारयन् ॥
16.25.m: They [gave] the dew-claws to Saramā; / to the tortoises they assigned the hooves; / his entrails to the worms / […] they held.

16.25.s: śṛṅgābhyāṃ rakṣa ṛṣaty arātiṃ hanti cakṣuṣā | śṛṇoti bhadraṃ karṇābhyāṃ gavāṃ yaḥ patir aghnyaḥ ||
16.25.d: शृङ्गाभ्यां रक्ष ऋषत्य् अरातिं हन्ति चक्षुषा । शृणोति भद्रं कर्णाभ्यां गवां यः पतिर् अघ्न्यः ॥
16.25.m: With his two horns he pierces the rakṣas; / with his eye he slays hostility; / with his ears he hears what is good— / he who is the lord of cows, not to be slain.

16.25.s: śatayājaṃ sa yajate nainaṃ dunvanty agnayaḥ | jinvanti sarve taṃ devā yo brāhmaṇa ṛṣabham ā juhoti ||
16.25.d: शतयाजं स यजते नैनं दुन्वन्त्य् अग्नयः । जिन्वन्ति सर्वे तं देवा यो ब्राह्मण ऋषभम् आ जुहोति ॥
16.25.m: He sacrifices […]; / the fires do not [consume] him; / all the gods quicken him / who offers up the bull to a Brahmin.

16.25.s: brāhmaṇāya vṛṣabhaṃ dattvā varīyaḥ kṛṇute manaḥ | puṣṭiṃ so aghnyānāṃ sve goṣṭhe vi paśyatu ||
16.25.d: ब्राह्मणाय वृषभं दत्त्वा वरीयः कृणुते मनः । पुष्टिं सो अघ्न्यानां स्वे गोष्ठे वि पश्यतु ॥
16.25.m: Having given a bull to a Brahmin, / one makes his mind broader. / Thriving may he / look upon in his own cattle-pen!

16.25.s: gāvaḥ santu prajāḥ santv atho astu tanūbalam | sarvaṃ tad anu manyantāṃ devā ṛṣabhadāyine ||
16.25.d: गावः सन्तु प्रजाः सन्त्व् अथो अस्तु तनूबलम् । सर्वं तद् अनु मन्यन्तां देवा ऋषभदायिने ॥
16.25.m: Let there be cows, let there be offspring, / and let there be bodily strength! / Let the gods assent to all that / for the giver of the bull!

16.26.s: ayaṃ pipāna indriyaṃ rayiṃ bibharti cetanīm | ayaṃ dhenuṃ sudughāṃ nityavatsāṃ vaśaṃ duhe vipaścitaṃ puro divaḥ ||
16.26.d: अयं पिपान इन्द्रियं रयिं बिभर्ति चेतनीम् । अयं धेनुं सुदुघां नित्यवत्सां वशं दुहे विपश्चितं पुरो दिवः ॥
16.26.m: He, swelling, bears / vital power [and] wealth. / He milks the cow of easy yield, of constant calf, / the wise barren cow, eastward from heaven.

16.26.s: piśaṅgarūpo nabhaso vayodhā aindraḥ śuṣmo viśvarūpo na āgan | prajām asmabhyaṃ dadhad rayiṃ ca rāyaspoṣam upasatvā sadema ||
16.26.d: पिशङ्गरूपो नभसो वयोधा ऐन्द्रः शुष्मो विश्वरूपो न आगन् । प्रजाम् अस्मभ्यं दधद् रयिं च रायस्पोषम् उपसत्वा सदेम ॥
16.26.m: Reddish-brown in form, bestower of vigor from the sky, / Indra's fury, of all forms, has come to us. / Bestowing offspring on us and wealth, / may we abide as attendants upon the thriving of wealth!

16.26.s: etaṃ vo yuvānaṃ pari dadhmo atra tena krīḍantīś carata vaśām̐ anu | mā no hiṃsiṣṭa januṣā subhāgā rāyaś ca poṣair abhi naḥ sacadhvam ||
16.26.d: एतं वो युवानं परि दध्मो अत्र तेन क्रीडन्तीश् चरत वशाँ अनु । मा नो हिंसिष्ट जनुषा सुभागा रायश् च पोषैर् अभि नः सचध्वम् ॥
16.26.m: We entrust this youth to you here; / sporting with him, range after the barren cows! / Do not harm us from birth, O fortunate ones, / and attend upon us with thrivings of wealth!

16.26.s: upehopaparcano 'smin goṣṭha upa pṛñcatu | upa ṛṣabhasya yad reta upendra tava vīryam ||
16.26.d: उपेहोपपर्चनो ऽस्मिन् गोष्ठ उप पृञ्चतु । उप ऋषभस्य यद् रेत उपेन्द्र तव वीर्यम् ॥
16.26.m: May the mingling [bull] / mingle here in this cattle-pen; / with what is the seed of the bull, / with [that], O Indra, [mingle] your virility!

16.27.s: ayaṃ pratisaro maṇir vīro vīrāya badhyate | vīryāvānt sapatnahā śūravīraḥ paripāṇaḥ sumaṅgalaḥ ||
16.27.d: अयं प्रतिसरो मणिर् वीरो वीराय बध्यते । वीर्यावान्त् सपत्नहा शूरवीरः परिपाणः सुमङ्गलः ॥
16.27.m: This amulet of counter-sorcery, / heroic, is bound for the hero: / full of virility, slayer of rivals, a hero of heroes, / an all-round protection, highly auspicious.

16.27.s: ayaṃ maṇiḥ sapatnahā suvīraḥ sahasvān vājī sahamāna ugraḥ | pratyak kṛtyā dūṣayann etu vīraḥ ||
16.27.d: अयं मणिः सपत्नहा सुवीरः सहस्वान् वाजी सहमान उग्रः । प्रत्यक् कृत्या दूषयन्न् एतु वीरः ॥
16.27.m: This amulet, slayer of rivals, giving good heroes, / powerful, victorious, overcoming, fierce— / turning back, spoiling sorceries, let the hero advance!

16.27.s: anenendro maṇinā vṛtram ahann anenāsurān parābhāvayan manīṣī | anena dyāvāpṛthivī ubhe ajayad anenājayat pradiśaś catasraḥ ||
16.27.d: अनेनेन्द्रो मणिना वृत्रम् अहन्न् अनेनासुरान् पराभावयन् मनीषी । अनेन द्यावापृथिवी उभे अजयद् अनेनाजयत् प्रदिशश् चतस्रः ॥

16.27.s: ayaṃ srāktyo maṇiḥ pratīvartaḥ pratisaraḥ | ojasvān vimṛdho maṇiḥ so asmān pātu viśvataḥ ||
16.27.d: अयं स्राक्त्यो मणिः प्रतीवर्तः प्रतिसरः । ओजस्वान् विमृधो मणिः सो अस्मान् पातु विश्वतः ॥
16.27.m:
This amulet of sraktya,
turning back [sorceries], counter-attacking,
vigorous, repelling foes—this amulet,
may it protect us from all sides.
